title.en: Volume 349 Biographies 108: Hao Zhi, Jia Kui, Dou Shunqing, Liu Changzuo, Lu Zheng, Yan Da, Yao Si and younger brother: Lin, sons: Xiong, Gu, Yang Sui, Liu Shunqing, Song Shouyue and son: Qiu
title.raw: 卷三百四十九 列傳第一百〇八 郝質 賈逵 竇舜卿 劉昌祚 盧政 燕達 姚兕弟:麟 子:雄 古 楊燧 劉舜卿 宋守約子:球 Volume 349 Biographies 108: Hao Zhi, Jia Kui, Dou Shunqing, Liu Changzuo, Lu Zheng, Yan Da, Yao Si and younger brother: Lin, sons: Xiong, Gu, Yang Sui, Liu Shunqing, Song Shouyue and son: Qiu

sentences.zh: 郝質 賈逵 竇舜卿 劉昌祚 盧政 燕達 姚兕弟:麟 子:雄 古 楊燧 劉舜卿 宋守約子:球

translations.literal: Hao Zhi, Jia Kui, Dou Shunqing, Liu Changzuo, Lu Zheng, Yan Da, Yao Si — younger brother: Lin, sons: Xiong, Gu, Yang Sui, Liu Shunqing, Song Shouyue — son: Qiu
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhi; Jia Kui; Dou Shunqing; Liu Changzuo; Lu Zheng; Yan Da; Yao Si, and his younger brother Lin; his sons Xiong and Gu; Yang Sui; Liu Shunqing; Song Shouyue and his son Qiu

sentences.zh: 郝質，字景純，汾州介休人。

translations.literal: Hao Zhi, courtesy name Jingchun, was a man of Jiexiu in Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhi, whose courtesy name was Jingchun, came from Jiexiu in Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，挽強為第一。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the army, and in drawing the strong bow he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army while still young and was unmatched in drawing the heavy bow.

sentences.zh: 充殿前行門，換供奉官，為府州駐泊都監，主管麟府軍馬，與田朏將兵護軍須饋麟州，道遇西夏數千騎寇鈔，質先驅力戰，斬首、獲馬數百。

translations.literal: He served as a gate guard of the Palace Directorate, exchanged his post for that of a Residency Attendant, became Garrison Supervisor stationed at Fuzhou, and oversaw the cavalry and horses of Lin Prefecture. With Tian Fei he led troops to escort military supplies to Lin Prefecture. On the road they encountered several thousand Western Xia horsemen raiding and plundering. Zhi took the lead and fought fiercely, beheading many and capturing several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Palace Directorate gate guard, then exchanged that post for a Residency Attendant commission and was made Garrison Supervisor at Fuzhou, in charge of the Lin Prefecture cavalry. With Tian Fei he led troops escorting army supplies to Lin Prefecture. On the march they met several thousand Western Xia horsemen on a looting raid. Zhi rode at the front and fought hard, killing many and seizing several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 又與朏行邊，至柏穀，敵塹道以阻官軍，質禦之於寒嶺下，轉鬥逐北，遂修復甯遠諸柵，以扼賊沖。

translations.literal: Again patrolling the frontier with Fei, they reached Bai Valley. The enemy dug trenches across the road to block the government army. Zhi held them off below Han Ridge, turned to fight and pursued the fleeing enemy northward, then restored the various stockades of Ningyuan to block the enemy's route of attack.
translations.idiomatic: On another frontier patrol with Fei they reached Bai Valley, where the enemy had dug trenches across the road to stop the imperial forces. Zhi held them at bay below Han Ridge, then turned, fought, and drove them north. He went on to rebuild the Ningyuan stockades and choke off the enemy's line of advance.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使杜衍、安撫使明鎬連薦之，且條上前後功狀，超遷內殿承制、並代路都監。

translations.literal: Commissioner Du Yan and Pacification Commissioner Ming Hao repeatedly recommended him and also itemized his achievements before and after; he was promoted beyond regular rank to Inner Hall Commissioner and Superintendent of the Bingdai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Du Yan and Pacification Commissioner Ming Hao recommended him again and again, setting out his record of service in detail. He was promoted ahead of schedule to Inner Hall Commissioner and Superintendent of the Bingdai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大名賈昌朝又薦為路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Jia Changchao of Daming also recommended him as Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Changchao of Daming also recommended him for appointment as Circuit Intendant.

sentences.zh: 使討貝州，文彥博至，命部城西。

translations.literal: When sent to suppress Beizhou, Wen Yanbo arrived and ordered him to encamp west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he was dispatched to suppress Beizhou, Wen Yanbo arrived and ordered his forces to take position west of the city.

sentences.zh: 回河上有亭甚壯，彥博慮為賊焚，遣小校藺千守，而質使千往他營度戰具，千辭，質曰：「亭焚，吾任其責。

translations.literal: On the river bend there was a very imposing pavilion. Yanbo feared the rebels would burn it and sent a junior officer, Lan Qian, to guard it. But Zhi sent Qian to another camp to survey battle equipment. Qian declined. Zhi said: "If the pavilion burns, I will bear the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: A fine pavilion stood on the bend of the river. Yanbo feared the rebels might burn it and posted a junior officer, Lan Qian, to guard it. Zhi then sent Qian to another camp to inspect the battle gear. When Qian refused, Zhi said, "If the pavilion burns, the blame is mine.

sentences.zh: 」千去而亭焚。

translations.literal: " Qian left, and the pavilion burned.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian went, and the pavilion was burned.

sentences.zh: 彥博將斬千，質趨至帳下曰：「千之去，質實使之，罪乃在質，願代千死。

translations.literal: Yanbo was about to execute Qian. Zhi hurried to the tent and said: "Qian's departure was in fact ordered by me. The guilt lies with Zhi. I wish to die in Qian's place.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was about to execute Qian. Zhi rushed to the command tent and said, "I am the one who sent Qian away. The fault is mine, and I ask to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 」彥博壯其義，兩釋之。

translations.literal: " Yanbo admired his righteousness and released them both.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanbo was moved by his sense of honor and released them both.

sentences.zh: 質自此益知名。

translations.literal: From this time Zhi became even more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zhi's reputation grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 質禦軍有紀律，犯者不貸，而享犒豐渥，公錢不足，出己奉助之。

translations.literal: In commanding troops Zhi was disciplined; offenders were not spared. Yet the rewards and feasts were generous. When public funds were insufficient, he drew on his own salary to supplement them.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded his troops with strict discipline and showed no mercy to offenders, yet he lavished rewards and feasts on his men. When the public funds ran short, he paid the difference out of his own salary.

sentences.zh: 平居自奉簡儉，食不重肉，篤于信義。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he kept himself frugal, never having two kinds of meat in a meal, and was deeply devoted to faith and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he lived simply, never serving more than one kind of meat at a meal, and he was steadfast in honor and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 田朏不振而死，為表揭前功，官其一孫。

translations.literal: Tian Fei died in reduced circumstances. Zhi memorialized to set forth his earlier achievements, and one of Fei's grandsons was given an official post.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Fei died in poverty and obscurity, Zhi submitted a memorial recounting his past service, and one of Fei's grandsons was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 在并州，與朝士董熙善，約為婚姻。

translations.literal: While in Bingzhou he was on good terms with the court gentleman Dong Xi and agreed to a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Bingzhou he became close to the court official Dong Xi, and the two arranged a marriage between their families.

sentences.zh: 熙死，家貧無依，質已為節度使，竟以女歸董氏。

translations.literal: Xi died, and his family was poor and without support. Zhi was already a military commissioner, yet in the end he gave his daughter in marriage to the Dong clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died, his family was left poor and without support. Though Zhi had by then become a military commissioner, he still gave his daughter in marriage to the Dong family as promised.

sentences.zh: 自為官，不上伐閱，從微至貴，皆以功次遷雲。

translations.literal: From the time he entered office he never boasted of his achievements. From humble rank to high honor, every promotion followed merit and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career he never trumpeted his own accomplishments. From the lowest ranks to the highest honors, every step came through merit and seniority alone.

sentences.zh: 賈逵，真定槁城人。

translations.literal: Jia Kui was a man of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui came from Gaocheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 隸拱聖為卒，至殿前班副都知，換西染院副使。

translations.literal: He was enrolled as a soldier in the Gongsheng Army, rose to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Directorate Guard, and exchanged his post for that of Vice Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a soldier in the Gongsheng Army, rose to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Directorate Guard, and then exchanged that post for a commission as Vice Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau.

sentences.zh: 從狄青征儂智高，戰於歸仁驛。

translations.literal: He followed Di Qing in the campaign against Nong Zhigao and fought at Guiren Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Di Qing against Nong Zhigao and fought at Guiren Post Station.

sentences.zh: 既陳，青誓眾曰：「不待令而舉者斬！

translations.literal: Once the battle line was formed, Qing swore to the army: "Whoever advances without awaiting the order shall be executed!
translations.idiomatic: Once the army was drawn up, Qing addressed the troops: "Anyone who moves before the order is given will be executed!

sentences.zh: 」時左將孫節戰死，逵為右將軍先鋒將，私念所部兵數困易衄，兵法先據高者勝，苟復待命而賊乘勝先登，吾事去矣。

translations.literal: " At that time the left general Sun Jie had died in battle. Kui was vanguard commander of the right wing. Privately he thought: the troops under my command have repeatedly suffered hardship and are easily routed. In the art of war, he who first occupies the high ground wins. If we again wait for orders and the enemy, riding their victory, seize the heights first, our cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: " By then the left-wing general Sun Jie had fallen in battle. Kui commanded the vanguard of the right wing. He thought to himself: his men had been worn down again and again and were prone to collapse. According to the art of war, victory goes to whoever holds the high ground first. If they waited again for orders while the enemy, emboldened by victory, seized the heights, all would be lost.

sentences.zh: 即日引軍趨山。

translations.literal: That very day he led his army toward the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he led his troops up the slope.

sentences.zh: 既定，賊至，逵麾眾馳下，仗劍大呼，斷賊為二。

translations.literal: Once the position was secured and the enemy arrived, Kui commanded his troops to charge down the slope. Brandishing his sword and shouting loudly, he cut the enemy force in two.
translations.idiomatic: When his men were in place and the enemy came up, Kui ordered a downhill charge. Sword in hand, he shouted and split the enemy column in two.

sentences.zh: 賊首尾不相救，遂潰。

translations.literal: Head and tail of the enemy could not aid each other, and they broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from one another, front and rear, the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 逵詣青請罪，青拊其背勞謝之。

translations.literal: Kui went to Qing to confess his offense. Qing clapped him on the back, praised him, and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Kui went to Qing to accept punishment. Qing clapped him on the back, praised his judgment, and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 邕州城空，青使逵入括公私遺墜，固辭。

translations.literal: Yongzhou city was empty. Qing ordered Kui to enter and collect public and private goods left behind, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou lay empty. Qing ordered Kui to enter the city and gather abandoned public and private property, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，將校多以搜城故匿竊金寶，獨逵無所犯。

translations.literal: At that time many officers and commanders, under the pretext of searching the city, secretly kept gold and jewels for themselves. Kui alone committed no offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officers used the city search as cover to keep gold and jewels for themselves. Kui alone took nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷西染院使、嘉州刺史、秦鳳路鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau, Prefect of Jiazhou, and Intendant of the Qinfeng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau, Prefect of Jia Prefecture, and Intendant of the Qinfeng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，逵少孤，厚賂繼父，得其母奉以歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kui had been orphaned in youth. He gave a large bribe to his stepfather and obtained his mother, whom he supported and brought home.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Kui had lost his father. He paid his stepfather a large sum, recovered his mother, and brought her home to support her.

sentences.zh: 至是，以母老辭，不許，而賜母冠帔。

translations.literal: By this time he pleaded to retire on account of his aged mother. The request was not granted, but his mother was bestowed a court lady's cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: Now he asked to retire because his mother was old. The court refused, but granted his mother the ceremonial cap and robe of a court lady.

sentences.zh: 秦山多巨木，與夏人錯壤，逵引輕兵往採伐。

translations.literal: Qin Mountain had many great trees, and its territory overlapped with that of the Xia people. Kui led light troops to go cut timber.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Mountain was rich in great timber, and its lands bordered those of the Xia. Kui led a light force there to harvest wood.

sentences.zh: 羌酋馳至，畫地立表約決勝負。

translations.literal: A Qiang chieftain galloped up, drew a line on the ground, set up a marker, and proposed to settle the outcome by contest.
translations.idiomatic: A Qiang chieftain rode up, marked out a line on the ground, and challenged him to settle the matter by contest.

sentences.zh: 逵引弓連三中的，酋下馬拜伏，從逵取盈而歸。

translations.literal: Kui drew his bow and hit the target three times in succession. The chieftain dismounted, bowed, and prostrated himself, then followed Kui and returned with a full load of timber.
translations.idiomatic: Kui drew his bow and hit the mark three times in a row. The chieftain dismounted, bowed to the ground, and then followed Kui back with a full load of timber.

sentences.zh: 徙並代路，專主管麟府軍馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Bingdai Circuit and placed solely in charge of the cavalry and horses of Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Bingdai Circuit and put in sole charge of the Lin Prefecture cavalry.

sentences.zh: 熟戶散處邊關，苦於寇略，逵差度遠近，聚為二十七堡，次第相望，自是害乃息。

translations.literal: Acculturated households were scattered along the border passes and suffered from raids and plunder. Kui assessed distances near and far and gathered them into twenty-seven forts, each in sight of the next. From then on the harm ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Acculturated frontier households were scattered along the passes and suffered constant raids. Kui measured distances and gathered them into twenty-seven forts, each within sight of the next. After that the raids largely stopped.

sentences.zh: 畫鐵為的，激種豪使射，久皆成勁兵。

translations.literal: He painted iron targets and stirred the tribal elites to shoot at them. In time they all became strong soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He set up iron targets and spurred the tribal leaders to practice archery. In time they all became crack troops.

sentences.zh: 一夕，烽火屢發，左右白當起，逵臥不應。

translations.literal: One night beacon fires were lit again and again. Those around him reported that he ought to rise, but Kui lay down and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: One night the beacon fires flared again and again. His attendants told him he should mobilize, but Kui stayed in bed and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 旦而謂人曰：「此必妄也。

translations.literal: At dawn he said to others: "This must be a false alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his men, "This has to be a false alarm.

sentences.zh: 脫有警，可夜出乎？

translations.literal: If there were truly an emergency, could one sortie by night?
translations.idiomatic: If there were a real attack, could we even sortie at night?

sentences.zh: 」徐問之，果邊人燭遺物也。

translations.literal: " When he questioned the matter at leisure, it turned out to be border people whose candles had ignited abandoned goods.
translations.idiomatic: " When he looked into it more closely, it turned out that frontier people had set fire to abandoned goods with their candles.

sentences.zh: 復徙秦鳳，去之十日，而代者郭恩敗。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Qinfeng. Ten days after he left, his replacement Guo En was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to Qinfeng. Ten days after he left, his successor Guo En suffered a defeat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以逵為能，連擢捧日天武四廂都指揮使、馬步殿前都虞候，曆涇原、高陽關、鄜延路副都總管，以利州觀察使入為步軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: The court regarded Kui as capable and promoted him in succession to Commander-in-Chief of the four companies of the Sun-supporting Heavenly Martial Guard, Chief Adjutant of the Cavalry and Infantry of the Palace Directorate, Deputy Overall Commander of the Jingyuan, Gaoyang Pass, and Fuyan circuits, and then, as Observation Commissioner of Lizhou, entered the capital as Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Kui highly capable and promoted him in quick succession: Commander-in-Chief of the four companies of the Sun-supporting Heavenly Martial Guard, Chief Adjutant of the Palace Cavalry and Infantry, Deputy Overall Commander on the Jingyuan, Gaoyang Pass, and Fuyan circuits, and finally, as Observation Commissioner of Li Prefecture, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Infantry in the capital.

sentences.zh: 都城西南水暴溢，注安上門，都水監以急變聞。

translations.literal: Southwest of the capital city the water suddenly overflowed in violence and poured toward Anshang Gate. The Directorate of Waterways reported the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Floods burst out southwest of the capital and surged toward Anshang Gate. The Directorate of Waterways reported the crisis.

sentences.zh: 英宗遣逵督護，亟囊土塞門，水乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong dispatched Kui to supervise the work. They quickly bagged earth to block the gate, and the water then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong sent Kui to take charge. His men quickly filled sacks with earth and blocked the gate, and the flood subsided.

sentences.zh: 議者欲穴堤以泄其勢，逵請觀水所行，諭居民徙高避水，然後決之。

translations.literal: Those in discussion wished to breach the dike to release its force. Kui asked to observe where the water would flow, instruct the residents to move to higher ground to avoid the water, and only then cut the dike.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers wanted to cut the dike to release the pressure. Kui asked first to trace the water's course, tell the residents to move to higher ground, and only then breach the dike.

sentences.zh: 軍校營城外者，每常朝，即未曉啟門鑰，或輟朝失報，啟鑰如平時。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers encamped outside the city, on every regular court day, would open the gate keys before dawn, or if court was suspended and no report came, would open the keys as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Officers camped outside the city would unlock the gates before dawn on every regular court day; if court was canceled and no notice came, they still opened them as usual.

sentences.zh: 逵言：「禁城當謹啟閉，不宜憑報者。

translations.literal: Kui said: "The forbidden city should be opened and closed with strict care. One should not rely on messengers.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "The imperial city must be opened and closed with strict discipline. We should not depend on word from messengers.

sentences.zh: 」乃冶鐵鑄「常朝」字，俾持以示信。

translations.literal: " He then smelted iron and cast the characters "Regular Court," so that holders could show them as proof.
translations.idiomatic: " He had iron cast with the characters for "Regular Court" so the bearer could show proof.

sentences.zh: 遷馬軍副都指揮使，復總鄜延兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Cavalry and again took overall command of the Fuyan forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Cavalry and again placed in overall command of the Fuyan army.

sentences.zh: 延州舊有夾河兩城，始，元吳入寇據險，城幾不能守。

translations.literal: Yanzhou formerly had two cities flanking the river. At first, when Yuan Hao invaded and seized the strategic heights, the cities were nearly impossible to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture had long had twin cities on either side of the river. When Yuan Hao invaded and seized the high ground, the cities were nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 逵相伏龍山、九州台之間可容窺覘，請於其地築保障，與城相望，延人以為便。

translations.literal: Kui surveyed the area between Fulong Mountain and Jiuzhou Terrace and found it suitable for observation. He requested that protective forts be built there, in sight of the cities. The people of Yanzhou regarded this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Kui found that the ground between Fulong Mountain and Jiuzhou Terrace offered good lines of sight and asked to build defensive posts there within view of the cities. The people of Yan Prefecture welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 轉昭信軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 逵言：「種諤處綏州降人於東偏，初雲萬三千戶，今乃千一百戶耳，逋逃之餘，所存才八百。

translations.literal: Kui said: "Zhong E settled the surrendered people of Suizhou on the eastern side. At first it was said there were thirteen thousand households; now there are only eleven hundred. After desertions and flight, those who remain are barely eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "Zhong E settled the Suizhou surrenderers on the eastern side. They were first said to number thirteen thousand households; now there are only eleven hundred. After desertions and flight, barely eight hundred remain.

sentences.zh: 蕃漢兩下殺傷，皆不啻萬計。

translations.literal: Casualties on both the tribal and Han sides alike were no less than tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Casualties on both the tribal and Han sides ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 自延州運粟至懷寧，率以四百錢致一石。

translations.literal: Transporting grain from Yanzhou to Huaining cost on average four hundred cash to deliver one shi.
translations.idiomatic: Moving grain from Yan Prefecture to Huaining cost on average four hundred cash per shi.

sentences.zh: 而緣邊居人，壯者但日給一升，罔冒何至大半。

translations.literal: Yet the frontier inhabitants received only one sheng per day for able-bodied men, and fraudulent claims amounted to more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Yet frontier residents were rationed only one sheng a day for each able-bodied man, and fraudulent claims consumed more than half the supply.

sentences.zh: 諤徒欲妄興邊事以自為功，不可不察也。

translations.literal: E and his faction wish recklessly to stir up frontier affairs to make merit for themselves. This cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: E and his followers want to stir up border trouble for their own credit. That cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 」元豐初，拜建武軍節度使、殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Jianwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: " At the start of the Yuanfeng era he was made Military Commissioner of the Jianwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 請不俟郊赦賜三世官，神宗曰：「逵武人，能有念親之志，其特許之。

translations.literal: He requested that offices be granted to three generations of his family without waiting for the suburban amnesty. Emperor Shenzong said: "Kui is a military man, yet he can cherish thoughts of honoring his kin. Let this be specially permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that offices be granted to three generations of his family without waiting for the suburban amnesty. Emperor Shenzong said, "Kui is a soldier, yet he still remembers his family. Grant his request.

sentences.zh: 」數月而卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: " Several months later he died, at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: " A few months later he died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，諡曰武恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Wuke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and given the posthumous name Wuke, "Steadfast in War."

sentences.zh: 竇舜卿

translations.literal: Dou Shunqing
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shunqing

sentences.zh: 竇舜卿，字希元，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Dou Shunqing, courtesy name Xiyuan, was a man of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shunqing, whose courtesy name was Xiyuan, came from Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以蔭為三班奉職，監平鄉縣酒稅。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a Third-Rank Attendant and supervised the wine tax of Pingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he received a Third-Rank Attendant appointment and supervised the wine tax at Pingxiang County.

sentences.zh: 有僧欲授以化汞為白金之術，謝曰：「吾祿足養親，不願學也。

translations.literal: A monk wished to teach him the art of turning mercury into white gold. He declined, saying: "My salary is sufficient to support my parents. I do not wish to learn it.
translations.idiomatic: A monk offered to teach him how to turn mercury into silver. He declined, saying, "My salary is enough to support my parents. I have no wish to learn that.

sentences.zh: 」辟府州兵馬監押。

translations.literal: " He was recruited as Supervisor of Cavalry and Horses at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Supervisor of Cavalry and Horses at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯塞，舜卿欲襲擊，舉烽求援于大將王凱，凱弗應。

translations.literal: When the Xia people violated the border, Shunqing wished to launch a surprise attack. He raised beacon fires to request aid from the great general Wang Kai, but Kai did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided the frontier, Shunqing wanted to counterattack. He lit the beacons and asked the senior general Wang Kai for help, but Kai did not respond.

sentences.zh: 舜卿度事急，提州兵出戰，勝之。

translations.literal: Shunqing judged the situation urgent, led out the prefectural troops to fight, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the situation urgent, Shunqing led the prefectural troops out and won the battle.

sentences.zh: 明日，經略使問狀，凱懼，要以同出為報。

translations.literal: The next day the frontier commissioner inquired into the affair. Kai was afraid and demanded that they report having sortied together.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the frontier commissioner asked for an account of the action. Kai, fearing blame, insisted they report that he had sortied with Shunqing.

sentences.zh: 舜卿歡然相許，不自以為功。

translations.literal: Shunqing gladly agreed and did not claim the achievement for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing agreed readily and did not claim the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 為青淄路都監。

translations.literal: He became Superintendent of the Qingzi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Superintendent of the Qingzi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 海盜行劫，執博昌鎮官吏，肆剽掠，舜卿募士三百，悉擒之。

translations.literal: Sea bandits went raiding, seized the officials of Bochang Town, and plundered at will. Shunqing recruited three hundred men and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sea pirates raided the coast, seized the officials of Bochang Town, and looted freely. Shunqing raised three hundred men and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，主客馬祐言：「昔先公客省善射，君當傳家法。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, the Master of Guests Ma You said: "In former days your late father, Guest of the Ministry of Rites, was skilled in archery. You ought to inherit the family method.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, the Master of Guests Ma You said, "Your late father, once a guest of the Ministry of Rites, was famed for his archery. You must carry on the family art.

sentences.zh: 」置酒請射，舜卿發輒中。

translations.literal: " He set out wine and invited him to shoot. Shunqing loosed an arrow and hit the mark every time.
translations.idiomatic: " He set out wine and invited him to shoot. Shunqing's every shot found its mark.

sentences.zh: 祐使奴持二弓示之，一挽皆折。

translations.literal: You had a servant bring out two bows to show him. Shunqing drew each one and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: You had a servant bring out two bows. Shunqing drew each one and snapped it.

sentences.zh: 湖北蠻徭彭仕羲叛，徙為鈐轄，兼知辰州。

translations.literal: In Hubei the Man and Yao chieftain Peng Shixi rebelled. Shunqing was transferred to be Circuit Intendant and concurrently Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Man and Yao chieftain Peng Shixi rebelled in Hubei, Shunqing was transferred to Circuit Intendant and concurrently made Prefect of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建請築州城，不擾而辦。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting the building of the prefectural city wall, and it was completed without disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to build the prefectural city walls, and the work was finished without troubling the populace.

sentences.zh: 帥師取富州，蠻將萬年州據石狗崖。

translations.literal: He led the army to take Fuzhou. The tribal general Wannianzhou held Shigou Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army to take Fu Prefecture, where the tribal general Wannianzhou held Shigou Cliff.

sentences.zh: 舜卿選壯卒奮擊，蠻矢石交下，卒蒙盾直前，發強弩射，萬年州斃於崖下，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Shunqing selected strong soldiers to press the attack fiercely. Tribal arrows and stones rained down. The soldiers shielded themselves and advanced straight ahead, then shot with powerful crossbows. Wannianzhou died below the cliff, and they took the position.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing chose his strongest men for a hard assault. Arrows and stones poured down from the cliff. His soldiers advanced under their shields, then loosed powerful crossbows. Wannianzhou was killed below the cliff, and the position was taken.

sentences.zh: 左右欲盡剿其眾，舜卿不許，曰：「仕羲願內附，特為此輩所脅，今死矣，何以多殺為？

translations.literal: Those around him wished to exterminate the whole force, but Shunqing would not allow it. He said: "Shixi wished to submit inwardly and was only coerced by this lot. Now that leader is dead, why further slaughter?
translations.idiomatic: His officers wanted to wipe out the whole force, but Shunqing refused. He said, "Shixi wanted to submit and was only forced along by these men. Their leader is dead now — why kill any more?

sentences.zh: 」引兵入北江，仕羲降。

translations.literal: " He led his troops into the Northern River region, and Shixi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched into the Northern River region, and Shixi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 擢康州刺史，加龍神衛、捧日天武四廂指揮使、馬軍殿前都虞候，三遷邕州觀察使，曆邠甯環慶路副都總管。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Prefect of Kangzhou, added as Commander of the Dragon Spirit Guard and Commander of the four companies of the Sun-supporting Heavenly Martial Guard, Chief Adjutant of the Cavalry of the Palace Directorate, thrice transferred to Observation Commissioner of Yongzhou, and served as Deputy Overall Commander of the Binning-Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Prefect of Kang Prefecture, made Commander of the Dragon Spirit Guard and of the four companies of the Sun-supporting Heavenly Martial Guard, Chief Adjutant of the Palace Cavalry, thrice promoted to Observation Commissioner of Yong Prefecture, and served as Deputy Overall Commander on the Binning-Huanqing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 熙甯中，十上章求退，且丐易文階。

translations.literal: During the Xining era he submitted ten memorials requesting retirement and also begged to exchange his rank for a civil grade.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he submitted ten memorials asking to retire and sought to exchange his military rank for a civil one.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎，提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Justice and made Superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Justice and Superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫致仕，再轉金紫光祿大夫，卒，年八十八。

translations.literal: He retired as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was again transferred to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and died at age eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was later promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and died at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康敏。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Kangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Kangmin, "Healthy and Keen."

sentences.zh: 劉昌祚

translations.literal: Liu Changzuo
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changzuo

sentences.zh: 劉昌祚，字子京，真定人。

translations.literal: Liu Changzuo, courtesy name Zijing, was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changzuo, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 父賀，戰沒於定川。

translations.literal: His father He died in battle at Dingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father He was killed in battle at Dingchuan.

sentences.zh: 錄為右班殿直，主秦州威遠砦。

translations.literal: Changzuo was enrolled as a Right-Rank Palace Attendant and placed in charge of Weiyuan Stockade in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo was granted a Right-Rank Palace Attendant appointment and put in charge of Weiyuan Stockade in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 青唐聚兵井鹽，經年不散。

translations.literal: The Qingtang tribes gathered troops at the salt wells and for a full year did not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtang tribesmen massed at the salt wells and held the ground for a full year.

sentences.zh: 昌祚奉帥命往詰之，諸酋曰：「聞漢家欲取吾鹽井。

translations.literal: Changzuo, on the commander's orders, went to question them. The chieftains said: "We have heard the Han court wishes to seize our salt wells.
translations.idiomatic: On his commander's orders Changzuo went to question them. The chieftains said, "We hear the Han court wants to take our salt wells.

sentences.zh: 」昌祚曰：「國家富有四海，何至與汝爭此邪？

translations.literal: " Changzuo said: "The state is rich in all within the four seas. Why would it stoop to contend with you over this?
translations.idiomatic: " Changzuo replied, "The empire owns all within the four seas. Why would it stoop to quarrel with you over this?

sentences.zh: 」與酋俱來，犒賚之，歡然帥眾去。

translations.literal: " He came back together with the chieftains, rewarded and gifted them, and they gladly led their followers away.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned with the chieftains, rewarded them generously, and they led their followers away in good spirits.

sentences.zh: 遷西路都巡檢。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Overall Inspector of the Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Overall Inspector of the Western Route.

sentences.zh: 使遼還，神宗臨試馳射，授通事舍人。

translations.literal: Returning from a mission to Liao, he was tested by Emperor Shenzong in mounted archery and was appointed Master of Ceremonies for Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from a mission to Liao, he was tested by Emperor Shenzong in mounted archery and appointed Master of Ceremonies for Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇劉溝堡，昌祚領騎二千出援。

translations.literal: When the Xia people raided Liugou Fort, Changzuo led two thousand horsemen out in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia attacked Liugou Fort, Changzuo led two thousand cavalry out to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 虜伏萬騎於黑山而偽遁，卒遇之，戰不解。

translations.literal: The enemy ambushed ten thousand horsemen at Black Mountain and feigned retreat; they suddenly encountered them, and the fighting did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had ten thousand horsemen lying in ambush at Black Mountain and feigned a retreat; when the two sides suddenly met, the fighting dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，大酋突而前，昌祚抽矢，一發殪之，餘眾悉遁。

translations.literal: Near dusk, a great chieftain suddenly pressed forward; Changzuo drew an arrow and killed him with one release; the remaining masses all fled.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a great chieftain charged forward; Changzuo nocked an arrow and dropped him with a single shot, and the rest fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 帥李師中上其功曰：「西事以來，以寡抗眾，未有如昌祚者。

translations.literal: The commander Li Shizhong submitted his merit and said: "Since the western affairs began, in using few to resist many, there has been none like Changzuo.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander Li Shizhong reported his achievement, saying, "Since the western campaigns began, no one has matched Changzuo in fighting a larger force with fewer men.

sentences.zh: 」知階州，討平毋家等族，又平疊州。

translations.literal: " He was made Intendant of Jie Prefecture, suppressed and pacified the Wujia and other clans, and also pacified Die Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed prefect of Jie Prefecture, where he suppressed the Wujia and other clans and also pacified Die Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉作坊使，為熙河路都監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Workshop Commissioner and served as Overall Supervisor of the Xihe Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Workshop Commissioner and Overall Supervisor of the Xihe Circuit.

sentences.zh: 從王中正入蜀，破篳篥羌。

translations.literal: Following Wang Zhongzheng he entered Shu and broke the Bili Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Zhongzheng into Shu and routed the Bili Qiang.

sentences.zh: 加皇城使、榮州刺史、秦鳳路鈐轄，又加西上閣門使、果州團練使，知河州。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Imperial City Commissioner, Prefect of Rong Prefecture, and Brigade Commander of the Qinfeng Circuit; again additionally made Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Militia Commissioner of Guo Prefecture, and Intendant of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Imperial City Commissioner, prefect of Rong Prefecture, and Brigade Commander of the Qinfeng Circuit, and later also made Western Upper Gate Commissioner, militia commissioner of Guo Prefecture, and prefect of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，為涇原副都總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, he became Deputy Overall Commander of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, he became deputy overall commander of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 王師西征，詔與總管姚麟率蕃漢兵五萬，受環慶高遵裕節制。

translations.literal: The royal army marched west; he was ordered together with Overall Commander Yao Lin to lead fifty thousand tribal and Han troops, subject to the command of Gao Zunyu of Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces marched west, an edict ordered him and overall commander Yao Lin to lead fifty thousand tribal and Han troops under the command of Gao Zunyu of Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 今兩路合軍以出，既入境，而慶兵不至。

translations.literal: Now the two routes combined armies to go out; having already entered the border, yet the Huanqing troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The two columns were to unite and advance together, but once they had crossed the border the Huanqing troops still had not appeared.

sentences.zh: 昌祚出胡盧川，次磨齊隘，夏眾十萬扼險不可前。

translations.literal: Changzuo went out through Huluchuan and halted at Moqi Pass; a hundred thousand Xia masses held the narrow defile and could not be advanced upon.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo advanced through Huluchuan and encamped at Moqi Pass, where a hundred thousand Xia troops blocked the defile and barred the way forward.

sentences.zh: 昌祚挾兩盾先登，夏人小卻，師乘之，斬首千七百級。

translations.literal: Changzuo, holding two shields, climbed first; the Xia people slightly withdrew; the army rode the momentum and beheaded one thousand seven hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo, wielding two shields, was first up the slope; the Xia fell back slightly, the army pressed in, and took seventeen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 進次鳴沙川，取其窖粟，遂薄靈州。

translations.literal: Advancing, he halted at Mingsha River, took their buried stored grain, and then drew near Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on to Mingsha River, seized their hidden grain stores, and advanced to the walls of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 城未及闔，先鋒奪門幾入，遵裕馳遣使止之，昌祚曰：「城不足下，脫朝廷謂我爭功，奈何？

translations.literal: The city had not yet been shut; the vanguard seized the gate and nearly entered; Zunyu urgently sent a messenger to stop them; Changzuo said: "The city is not sufficient to be taken; if the court should say we vied for merit, what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Before the gates could be shut, the vanguard almost burst through; Zunyu sent a messenger at full gallop to halt them. Changzuo said, "The city cannot be taken in time—and if the court accuses us of competing for credit, what then?

sentences.zh: 」命按甲勿攻。

translations.literal: " He ordered to hold armor and not attack.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the men to stand down and not assault the walls.

sentences.zh: 是夕，慶兵始距城三十里而軍，遇敵接戰，昌祚遣數千騎赴之。

translations.literal: That evening, the Huanqing troops for the first time encamped thirty li from the city and battled the enemy in engagement; Changzuo sent several thousand horsemen to go to them.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Huanqing troops at last made camp thirty li from the city, clashed with the enemy, and Changzuo sent several thousand cavalry to their relief.

sentences.zh: 遲明，賊已退，遂謁遵裕，遵裕訝應援之緩，有誅昌祚意。

translations.literal: At late dawn, the bandits had already retreated; he then paid a visit to Zunyu; Zunyu was surprised at the slowness of the relief and had an intent to execute Changzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Near daybreak the enemy had already withdrawn; Changzuo went to see Zunyu, who was angered by the tardy relief and meant to have Changzuo put to death.

sentences.zh: 既見，問下城如何，昌祚曰：「比欲攻城，以幕府在後未敢。

translations.literal: Once he saw him, he asked how taking the city went; Changzuo said: "Just now I wished to assault the city, but because the headquarters was in the rear I did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: When they met, Zunyu asked why the city had not been taken. Changzuo said, "I had meant to storm it, but with your headquarters still behind me I did not dare.

sentences.zh: 前日磨齊之戰，夏眾退保東關，若乘銳破之，城必自下。

translations.literal: At the battle of Moqi the day before, the Xia masses retreated to hold East Gate; if riding the sharp edge to break them, the city would certainly fall of itself.
translations.idiomatic: At Moqi the Xia fell back to East Gate—if we had struck while their spirit was broken, the city would have surrendered itself.

sentences.zh: 」遵裕弗內，曰：「吾夜以萬人負土囊傅壘，至旦入矣。

translations.literal: " Zunyu did not accept it inwardly, saying: "I by night used ten thousand men carrying earth bags to build against the ramparts; by dawn we would have entered.
translations.idiomatic: " Zunyu would not hear of it and said, "I was preparing to have ten thousand men carry sacks of earth and raise the ramparts overnight—we would have been inside by dawn.

sentences.zh: 」怒未解，欲奪其兵付姚麟，麟不敢受，乃已。

translations.literal: " His anger had not yet been released; he wished to seize his troops and hand them to Yao Lin; Lin did not dare accept, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Still furious, he tried to strip Changzuo of command and transfer the troops to Yao Lin, but Lin declined to accept, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明日，遣昌祚巡營，凡所得馬糧，悉為慶兵所取，涇師忿噪。

translations.literal: The next day, he sent Changzuo to patrol the camps; whatever horses and grain were obtained were entirely taken by the Huanqing troops; the Jing troops angrily clamored.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent Changzuo to inspect the camps, but every horse and ration seized was taken by the Huanqing troops, and the Jing soldiers erupted in outrage.

sentences.zh: 遵裕圍城十八日，不能下，夏人決七級渠以灌遵裕師，軍遂潰。

translations.literal: Zunyu besieged the city eighteen days and could not take it; the Xia people broke the Seven-Level Canal to flood Zunyu's army; the army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyu besieged the city for eighteen days without success; the Xia breached the Seven-Level Canal and flooded his camp, and the army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 即南還，復命涇師為殿。

translations.literal: Immediately they returned south; again he ordered the Jing troops to serve as the rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew south at once, and once again the Jing troops were ordered to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 昌祚手劍水上，待眾濟然後行，為虜所及，戰退之。

translations.literal: Changzuo, sword in hand at the water, waited for the masses to cross before going; he was caught by the enemy and fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo stood in the water with his sword drawn, holding the crossing until every man was over before he moved; the enemy caught up and he fought them off.

sentences.zh: 至渭州，糧盡，士爭入，無復行伍，坐貶永興軍鈐轄。

translations.literal: Reaching Weizhou, grain was exhausted; soldiers scrambled to enter; there were no longer ranks; for this he was demoted to Brigade Commander of Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Weizhou the food was gone; soldiers fought to get inside the walls and the columns dissolved entirely, for which he was demoted to Brigade Commander of the Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，復徙涇原，加龍、神衛四廂都指揮使，知延州。

translations.literal: The next year, he was again transferred to Jingyuan; additionally made Overall Commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard; Intendant of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred back to Jingyuan, promoted to Overall Commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard, and made prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時永樂方陷，士氣不振，昌祚先修馬政，令軍中校技擊，優者乃給焉。

translations.literal: At the time Yongle had just fallen and troop spirit was not raised; Changzuo first reformed horse policy; he ordered the army to test martial skills; only the superior were then given them.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle had just fallen and morale was shattered; Changzuo first overhauled the horse policy, requiring troops to compete in martial skill—only the best were issued mounts.

sentences.zh: 自義合至德靖砦，綿互七百里，堡壘疏密不齊，烽燧不相應。

translations.literal: From Yihe to Dejing Stockade, extending seven hundred li, fortresses and ramparts were sparse and dense without uniformity; beacon fires did not correspond.
translations.idiomatic: From Yihe to Dejing Stockade the line ran seven hundred li, with forts unevenly spaced and beacons that could not signal one another.

sentences.zh: 昌祚度屯戍險易、地望遠近、事力強弱，立為定式，上諸朝。

translations.literal: Changzuo measured stationed garrisons' difficulty and ease, terrain's near and far vantage, and the strength and weakness of resources; established them as fixed standards; submitted them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo surveyed each post for terrain, distance, and available strength, drew up fixed standards, and submitted the plan to court.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇塞門、安遠砦，拒破之，殺其統軍葉悖麻、咩吪埋二人，蓋始謀攻永樂者。

translations.literal: The Xia people raided Saimen and Anyuan stockades; he repulsed and broke them; killed their commanders-in-chief Ye Poma and Mie'aimai, the two who had first plotted to attack Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia attacked Saimen and Anyuan stockades he drove them off and killed their generals Ye Poma and Mie'aimai—the very men who had first planned the strike on Yongle.

sentences.zh: 圖其形以獻。

translations.literal: He drew their likenesses and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He had portraits drawn and sent them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，遣近侍勞軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and sent a close attendant to comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and sent a palace attendant to congratulate the troops.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，進步軍都虞候、雄州團練使、知渭州，曆馬軍殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: When Zhezong was enthroned, he advanced to Adjutant of the Foot Army, Militia Commissioner of Xiong Prefecture, Intendant of Wei Prefecture; successively served as Adjutant of the Mounted Army in the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, Changzuo was promoted to Adjutant of the Foot Army, militia commissioner of Xiong Prefecture, and prefect of Wei Prefecture, and later served as Adjutant of the Mounted Army at the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 渭地宜牧養，故時弓箭手人授田二頃，有馬者復增給之，謂之「馬口分地」。

translations.literal: Wei territory was suited for pasturing and raising; therefore in former times each bowman was granted two qing of land; those with horses were further additionally granted land—this was called "Horse-Quota Allotted Land."
translations.idiomatic: Wei was good grazing country; bowmen had once been granted two qing apiece, with extra allotments for those who kept horses—a system called "horse-quota land."

sentences.zh: 其後馬死不補，而據地自若。

translations.literal: Afterward, when horses died they were not replenished, yet they held the land as of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when horses died they were not replaced, yet the holders kept the land anyway.

sentences.zh: 昌祚按舉其法，不二年，耗為復初。

translations.literal: Changzuo investigated and upheld the law; within two years, depletion returned to the original state.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo investigated and enforced the regulations; within two years the system was restored to what it had been.

sentences.zh: 又括隴山間田得萬頃，募士卒五千，別置將統之，勁悍出諸軍右。

translations.literal: Further, he requisitioned land between Long Mountains obtaining ten thousand qing; recruited five thousand soldiers; separately appointed generals to command them; fierce and bold beyond all armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also consolidated ten thousand qing of farmland in the Long Mountains, recruited five thousand soldiers under specially appointed commanders, and trained a force fiercer than any in the region.

sentences.zh: 朝廷歸夏人四砦，昌祚以為不可。

translations.literal: The court returned four stockades to the Xia people; Changzuo considered it unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned four stockades to the Xia, Changzuo argued that it was a mistake.

sentences.zh: 再遷殿前副都指揮使、冀州觀察使、武康軍節度使。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Deputy Overall Commander before the Palace, Observation Commissioner of Ji Prefecture, Military Commissioner of the Wukang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Deputy Overall Commander of the Palace Guard, observation commissioner of Ji Prefecture, and military commissioner of the Wukang Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died, age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡曰毅肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Master of the State with Equal Honors to the Three Excellencies; posthumous name Yisu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the State with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Yisu, "Resolute and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 昌祚氣貌雄偉，最善騎射，箭出百步之外。

translations.literal: Changzuo's spirit and appearance were grand and imposing; he was best at mounted archery; arrows went beyond a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo was imposing in bearing and unmatched in mounted archery—his arrows carried more than a hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 夏人得箭以為神，持歸事之。

translations.literal: The Xia people who obtained his arrows regarded them as divine; took them home and served them.
translations.idiomatic: Xia warriors who recovered his arrows treated them as sacred relics and carried them home as objects of veneration.

sentences.zh: 所著《射法》行於世。

translations.literal: His composed 《Archery Methods》 circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His treatise 《Archery Methods》 circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 盧政，太原文水人。

translations.literal: Lu Zheng, a man of Wenshui in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zheng was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以神衛都頭從劉平與夏人戰延州。

translations.literal: As company leader of the Divine Guard he followed Liu Ping to battle the Xia people at Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a company leader in the Divine Guard he served under Liu Ping against the Xia at Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 虜薄西南隅，兵不得成列，政引數騎挑戰，發伏弩二百射卻之。

translations.literal: The enemy pressed the southwest corner; troops could not form ranks; Zheng led several horsemen to challenge; released two hundred hidden crossbows and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy pressed the southwest corner and the lines could not hold, Zheng led a few horsemen out to challenge them and drove them back with two hundred hidden crossbows.

sentences.zh: 日且暮，政說平曰：「今處山間，又逼汙澤，宜速退保後山，須明決鬥；

translations.literal: The day was nearly dusk; Zheng persuaded Ping, saying: "Now we are in the mountains and also pressed against a muddy marsh; we ought quickly to withdraw and hold the rear mountain; we must at dawn decide the battle;
translations.idiomatic: As dusk approached, Zheng urged Ping, "We are in the hills and trapped against a swamp—we should fall back at once and hold the high ground to the rear, and only settle this at dawn in open battle;

sentences.zh: 不然，彼夜出，乘高蹙我，何以禦之？

translations.literal: Otherwise, if they come out by night, riding the heights to press us—how can we repel them?
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they will strike by night from above and crush us—how will we hold them off?

sentences.zh: 」平不聽，遂敗。

translations.literal: " Ping did not listen, and so they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " Ping would not listen, and they were routed.

sentences.zh: 政脫身歸，黃德和誣平降賊，仁宗引政問狀，政言：「平被執，非降也。

translations.literal: Zheng escaped and returned; Huang Dehe falsely accused Ping of surrendering to the bandits; Emperor Renzong summoned Zheng to ask the circumstances; Zheng said: "Ping was seized—it was not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng got away and reported back; Huang Dehe accused Liu Ping of defecting to the enemy. Emperor Renzong summoned Zheng to testify, and Zheng said, "Ping was captured—it was not a surrender.

sentences.zh: 」因自陳失主將當死。

translations.literal: " He further declared himself that losing the commander ought to mean death.
translations.idiomatic: " He added that having lost his commander, he deserved to die.

sentences.zh: 帝義其言，赦之，以為供奉官、德州兵馬監押。

translations.literal: The Emperor found righteousness in his words, pardoned him, and made him Palace Attendant and Military Supervisor of De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his loyalty, pardoned him, and appointed him Palace Attendant and military supervisor of De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 預討貝州，率勇敢數百人，飛繯絓堞而登，守者莫能亢，大軍乘之以入。

translations.literal: Participating in the campaign against Bei Prefecture, he led several hundred brave men; flying grappling hooks caught the battlements and they climbed; defenders could not resist; the great army rode the opportunity to enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Bei Prefecture he led several hundred picked men who scaled the walls with grappling hooks; the defenders could not stop them, and the main force poured in behind.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿承制。

translations.literal: Transferred to Inner Palace Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Inner Palace Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 南征儂智高，亦有功。

translations.literal: In the southern campaign against Nong Zhigao, he also had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also distinguished himself in the southern campaign against Nong Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 曆秦鳳、高陽關都鈐轄。

translations.literal: Successively served as Brigade Commander of Qinfeng and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Brigade Commander of Qinfeng and of Gaoyang Pass in turn.

sentences.zh: 治平、熙寧中，為捧日、天武四廂都指揮使三衛都虞候、副都指揮使，涇原、定州、並代、真定四路副都總管，累轉祁州團練、昌州防禦、黔州觀察使。

translations.literal: During Zhiping and Xining, he was Overall Commander of the four wings of the Sun-Bearer and Heaven-Warrior Guards, Adjutant of the Three Guards, Deputy Overall Commander; Deputy Overall Commander of the four routes Jingyuan, Ding Prefecture, Bingdai, and Zhending; repeatedly transferred to Militia Commissioner of Qi Prefecture, Defense Commissioner of Chang Prefecture, Observation Commissioner of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Yingzong and Shenzong he rose to Overall Commander of the Sun-Bearer and Heaven-Warrior Guards, Adjutant of the Three Guards and deputy overall commander, and deputy overall commander of the Jingyuan, Dingzhou, Bingdai, and Zhending circuits, eventually becoming militia commissioner of Qi Prefecture, defense commissioner of Chang Prefecture, and observation commissioner of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 拜武泰軍節度使，政時年七十三，氣貌不衰，侍立殿下，雖久無惰容，能上馬踴躍，觀者壯之。

translations.literal: Appointed Military Commissioner of the Wutai Army; Zheng was then age seventy-three; spirit and appearance undiminished; standing in attendance below the hall, though long without a weary expression; could mount a horse and leap; onlookers found him strong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Wutai Army at the age of seventy-three, still vigorous in bearing; he could stand on ceremony for hours without tiring, mount a horse with a spring in his step—and those who watched admired his stamina.

sentences.zh: 早朝暴卒，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At early court audience he suddenly died; posthumously granted Grand Master of the State with Equal Honors to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly while attending early court and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the State with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 燕達，字逢辰，開封人。

translations.literal: Yan Da, courtesy name Fengchen, a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Da, courtesy name Fengchen, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，與儕輩戲，輒為軍陳行列狀，長老異之。

translations.literal: When a child, playing with his peers, always made military formations and ranks; elders found him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy at play with his companions he would always set out mock battle lines; the elders thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 既長，容體魁梧，善騎射。

translations.literal: Once grown, stature imposing, skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was tall and powerfully built, and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 以材武隸禁籍，授內殿崇班，為延州巡檢，戍懷寧砦。

translations.literal: For talent and martial skill enrolled in the forbidden roster; granted Inner Palace Honorary Attendant; made Inspector of Yan Prefecture; garrisoned Huaining Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: His ability earned him a place in the palace guard rolls; he was made an Honorary Attendant of the Inner Palace, appointed inspector of Yan Prefecture, and posted to Huaining Stockade.

sentences.zh: 夏人三萬騎薄城，戰竟日不決，達所部止五百人，躍馬奮擊，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand Xia horsemen pressed the city; they fought all day without resolution; Da's unit had only five hundred men; leaping on horse he fought fiercely; wherever he went none withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand Xia cavalry pressed the walls; the fighting lasted all day without decision. Da had only five hundred men under his command, yet he charged in wherever he rode and broke every line he met.

sentences.zh: 擢鄜延都監，數帥兵深入敵境，九戰皆以勝歸。

translations.literal: Promoted to Overall Supervisor of Fuyan; several times led troops deep into enemy territory; nine battles all with victory returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Overall Supervisor of the Fuyan circuit and repeatedly led raids deep into enemy country—nine engagements, nine victories.

sentences.zh: 囉兀之棄走，遣達援取戍卒輜重，為賊所邀，且戰且南，失亡頗多。

translations.literal: At Luowu's abandoning flight, Da was dispatched to rescue and recover garrison troops and baggage; was intercepted by bandits; fought while going south; losses were considerable.
translations.idiomatic: When Luowu was abandoned and the garrison fled, Da was sent to retrieve the men and their baggage; the enemy waylaid him, and he fought his way south with heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 神宗以達孤軍遇敵，所全亦不為少，累遷西上閣門使、領英州刺史，為秦鳳副總管。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong, considering Da's isolated army meeting the enemy—what he preserved was not small—repeatedly promoted him to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, concurrently Prefect of Ying Prefecture, Deputy Overall Commander of Qinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong noted that Da, fighting alone against the enemy, had still saved a substantial force, and promoted him repeatedly—to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, acting prefect of Ying Prefecture, and deputy overall commander of Qinfeng.

sentences.zh: 討破河州羌，遂降木征。

translations.literal: He campaigned and broke the He Prefecture Qiang; thereby Muzheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the He Prefecture Qiang and accepted the surrender of Muzheng.

sentences.zh: 遷東上閣門使、副都總管，真拜忠州刺史、龍神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, Deputy Overall Commander; formally appointed Prefect of Zhong Prefecture, Overall Commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and deputy overall commander, then formally appointed prefect of Zhong Prefecture and Overall Commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 郭逵招討安南，為行營馬步軍副都總管。

translations.literal: Guo Kui as Pacification Commissioner of Annan; he served as Deputy Overall Commander of the Field Army's Horse and Foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Kui was appointed to pacify Annam, Da served as his deputy overall commander of the field army, horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 入辭，神宗諭之曰：「卿名位已重，不必親矢石，第激勉將土可也。

translations.literal: Entering to take leave, Emperor Shenzong instructed him: "Your fame and rank are already heavy; you need not personally face arrows and stones; merely rouse and encourage the generals and troops.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave of the throne, Emperor Shenzong told him, "Your rank is high enough—you need not expose yourself to arrow and stone; stir up the troops and that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」達頓首謝曰：「臣得憑威靈滅賊，雖死何憚！

translations.literal: " Da kowtowed and thanked, saying: "Your servant, relying on your power to destroy the bandits—even death, what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: " Da kowtowed and replied, "If I may borrow Your Majesty's majesty to crush the enemy, what is death to me?

sentences.zh: 」初度嶺，聞前鋒遇敵苦戰，欲往援，偏校有言當先為家計然後進者，達曰：「彼戰已危，詎忍為自全計。

translations.literal: " Just after crossing the mountains, he heard the vanguard met the enemy in bitter fighting and wished to go to their relief; a junior officer said one ought first to plan for the household and then advance; Da said: "Their battle is already perilous—how can I bear to plan for self-preservation?
translations.idiomatic: " Just after crossing the mountains he learned the vanguard was locked in fierce combat and meant to ride to their aid. A junior officer argued they ought to secure camp first; Da said, "They are already in mortal danger—how could I think only of saving myself?

sentences.zh: 」下令敢言安營者斬。

translations.literal: " He ordered: whoever dares speak of establishing camp will be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered that anyone who spoke of making camp would be executed.

sentences.zh: 乃卷甲趨之，士皆自奮，傳呼太尉來，蠻驚潰，即定廣源。

translations.literal: Then with armor rolled up they hurried thither; the troops all exerted themselves; the cry passed that the Grand Marshal had come; the barbarians were startled and routed; immediately pacified Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He marched at once without pause; the men fought as if possessed, and at the shout that the Grand Marshal had arrived the enemy broke and fled—Guangyuan was secured on the spot.

sentences.zh: 師次富良江，蠻艤鬥船于南岸，欲戰不得，達默計曰：「兵法致人而不致於人，吾示之以虛，彼必來戰。

translations.literal: The army halted at the Fu River; the barbarians moored fighting ships on the south bank; wishing to fight but unable; Da silently calculated: "In the art of war one brings others and is not brought by others—I will show them emptiness; they will surely come to battle.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped on the Fu River, where the enemy had warships anchored on the south bank beyond reach. Da reflected silently: "The art of war is to make the enemy come to you—to lure them I will feign weakness, and they will attack.

sentences.zh: 」已而蠻果來，擊之，大敗，乃請降。

translations.literal: " Before long the barbarians indeed came; he struck them and greatly defeated them; they then requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the enemy did come; he struck and routed them, and they sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 師還，拜榮州防禦使。

translations.literal: The army returned; appointed Defense Commissioner of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made defense commissioner of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以主帥得罪而獨蒙賞，乞同責，不聽。

translations.literal: Because the supreme commander was punished for an offense yet he alone received reward; he requested shared punishment; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because the commanding general had been punished while he alone was rewarded, he asked to share in the blame; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，遷金州觀察使，加步軍都虞候，改馬軍，超授副都指揮使。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, transferred to Observation Commissioner of Jin Prefecture; promoted to Adjutant of the Foot Army; changed to the Mounted Army; exceptionally granted Deputy Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era he became observation commissioner of Jin Prefecture, was made Adjutant of the Foot Army and then of the Mounted Army, and was raised directly to Deputy Overall Commander.

sentences.zh: 以訓閱精整，除一子閣門祗候。

translations.literal: For training and inspection being precise and orderly, one son was appointed Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because his troops drilled to exceptional order, one of his sons was appointed a Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 數被詔獎，進殿前副都指揮使、武康軍節度使。

translations.literal: Repeatedly rewarded by imperial edict; promoted to Deputy Overall Commander before the Palace, Military Commissioner of the Wukang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly commended by imperial decree and promoted to Deputy Overall Commander of the Palace Guard and military commissioner of the Wukang Army.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，遷為使，徙節武信。

translations.literal: When Zhezong was enthroned, he was transferred to Commissioner; moved his commission to Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, he was made Military Commissioner and transferred his commission to Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰毅敏。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Grand Master of the State with Equal Honors to the Three Excellencies; posthumous name Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the State with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Yimin, "Resolute and Keen."

sentences.zh: 達起行伍，喜讀書，神宗以其忠實可任，每燕見，未嘗不從容。

translations.literal: Da rose from the ranks, enjoyed reading books; Emperor Shenzong, finding him loyal and trustworthy and capable of appointment, at every banquet audience was always at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Da had risen from the ranks yet loved learning; Emperor Shenzong found him steadfast and reliable, and at every private audience spoke with him at length.

sentences.zh: 嘗問：「用兵當何先？

translations.literal: He once asked: "In using troops, what ought to come first?
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the emperor asked, "What should come first in the use of troops?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「莫如愛。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Nothing like love.
translations.idiomatic: " Da answered, "Nothing is more important than caring for the men.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「威克厥愛可乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Can severity overcome that love?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "May stern discipline override such care?

sentences.zh: 」達曰：「威非不用，要以愛為先耳。

translations.literal: " Da said: "Severity is not that it is unused—it is just that love must come first.
translations.idiomatic: " Da replied, "Sternness has its place—but care for the men must come first.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 姚兕，字武之，五原人。

translations.literal: Yao Si, courtesy name Wuzhi, a man of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Si, courtesy name Wuzhi, was a native of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 父寶，戰死定川，兕補右班殿直，為環慶巡檢。

translations.literal: His father Bao died in battle at Dingchuan; Si was enrolled as Right-Rank Palace Attendant and made Inspector of Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao was killed at Dingchuan; Si entered service as a Right-Rank Palace Attendant and was posted as inspector of Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 與夏人戰，一矢斃其酋，眾潰，因乘之，遂破蘭浪。

translations.literal: Battling the Xia people, one arrow killed their chieftain; the masses routed; riding the momentum he broke Lanlang.
translations.idiomatic: In a fight with the Xia he dropped their chieftain with a single arrow; the enemy scattered, and he pressed the rout until Lanlang fell.

sentences.zh: 敵大舉寇邊，諸砦皆受圍。

translations.literal: The enemy on a grand scale raided the border; all stockades received siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy invaded in force, every stockade came under siege.

sentences.zh: 兕時駐荔原堡，先羌未至，據險張疑兵，伺便輒出。

translations.literal: Si was then stationed at Liyuan Fort; before the Qiang arrived, he held strategic positions and spread a deceptive force; whenever convenient he sallied forth.
translations.idiomatic: Si was holding Liyuan Fort; before the Qiang arrived he occupied the high ground, feigned a larger force, and sallied whenever he saw an opening.

sentences.zh: 有悍酋臨陣甚武，兕前射中其目，斬首還，一軍歡呼。

translations.literal: There was a fierce chieftain very martial at the battle line; Si rode forward, shot him in the eye, beheaded him and returned; the whole army cheered.
translations.idiomatic: A ferocious enemy chieftain was fighting at the front; Si rode out, put an arrow through his eye, took his head, and rode back to a cheer from the whole garrison.

sentences.zh: 明日，來攻益急，兕手射數百人，裂指流血。

translations.literal: The next day, they came to attack with increasing urgency; Si personally shot several hundred men; his fingers split and bled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the assault grew fiercer; Si shot down hundreds of men himself until his fingers split and ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 又遣子雄引壯騎馳掩其後，所向必克。

translations.literal: Further he dispatched his son Xiong to lead elite horsemen in a swift raid on their rear; wherever they went they were sure to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his son Xiong at the head of picked cavalry to sweep around behind the enemy—and every charge broke through.

sentences.zh: 敵度不可破，乃退攻大順城。

translations.literal: The enemy judged [the position] could not be broken, so [they] withdrew and attacked Dashun Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they could not break through, the enemy pulled back and turned instead on Dashun Fort.

sentences.zh: 兕復往救，轉鬥三日，凡斬級數千，卒全二城。

translations.literal: Si again went to rescue; turning and fighting for three days, in all beheading ranks by the thousands, finally preserving both cities entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Si marched to relieve them again. For three days the battle seesawed; he took several thousand heads and at last saved both cities.

sentences.zh: 慶軍叛，兕以親兵守西關，盜眾不得入而奔。

translations.literal: The Qing army rebelled; Si with personal troops guarded the western pass, the bandit masses could not enter and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing garrison mutinied, Si held the western gate with his personal guard. The rebels could not get in and broke away in flight.

sentences.zh: 兕追及，下馬與語，皆感泣羅拜，誓無復為亂。

translations.literal: Si pursued and caught up, dismounted and spoke with them; all were moved to tears and bowed in a ring, swearing never again to make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He overtook them, dismounted, and spoke to them face to face. They wept and prostrated themselves in a circle, vowing never to rebel again.

sentences.zh: 神宗聞其名，召入覲，試以騎射，屢中的，賜銀槍、袍帶。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong heard his name, summoned him to audience, tested him in mounted archery—repeatedly hitting the mark—and bestowed a silver spear, robe, and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong heard of him and summoned him to court. He tested Si in horsemanship and archery; Si hit the target again and again. The emperor rewarded him with a silver spear, robe, and belt.

sentences.zh: 遷為路都監，徙鄜延、涇原。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be circuit intendant, and moved to Fuyan and Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit intendant and transferred in turn to the Fuyan and Jingyuan commands.

sentences.zh: 從攻河州，飛矢貫耳，戰益力。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Hezhou, a flying arrow pierced his ear; he fought with increased force.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Hezhou a stray arrow drove through his ear, yet he fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 河州既得，又為鬼章所圍，兕曰：「解圍之法，當攻其所必救。

translations.literal: Once Hezhou was taken, [he] was again besieged by Gui Zhang. Si said: "The method to lift a siege is to strike what the enemy must rescue.
translations.idiomatic: After Hezhou fell, Gui Zhang surrounded him in turn. Si said, "To break a siege you must hit what the enemy cannot afford to lose.

sentences.zh: 」乃往擊隴宗，圍遂解。

translations.literal: " He then went to strike Longzong, and the siege was thereupon lifted.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched against Longzong, and the encirclement dissolved.

sentences.zh: 累遷皇城使，進鈐轄。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached Imperial City Commissioner and advanced to Controller.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted step by step, he rose to Imperial City Commissioner and then to Controller.

sentences.zh: 從攻交阯有功，領雅州刺史。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Jiaozhi with merit, he headed Yazhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He served with distinction in the campaign against Jiaozhi and was appointed prefect of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 破乞弟，領忠州團練使，進副總管，遷東上閣門使，徙熙河。

translations.literal: Defeating Qidi, he headed Zhongzhou as regimentation commissioner, advanced to deputy chief commander, was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, and moved to Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Qidi he was made regimentation commissioner of Zhongzhou, then deputy chief commander, Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, and finally transferred to Xihe.

sentences.zh: 與種誼合兵討鬼章於洮州，破六逋宗城，夜斷浮橋，援兵不得度，遂擒鬼章。

translations.literal: Joining forces with Chong Yi to punish Gui Zhang at Taozhou, they broke Liupuzong City, by night cut the pontoon bridge so relief troops could not cross, and thereupon captured Gui Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He united with Chong Yi to campaign against Gui Zhang at Taozhou. They stormed Liupuzong City, severed the floating bridge by night so reinforcements could not cross, and took Gui Zhang captive.

sentences.zh: 真拜通州團練使。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed regimentation commissioner of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received formal appointment as regimentation commissioner of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒于鄜延總管，贈忠州防禦使。

translations.literal: He died while chief commander of Fuyan; posthumously [honored as] defense commissioner of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as chief commander of Fuyan and was posthumously enfeoffed as defense commissioner of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 兕幼失父，事母孝，凡圖畫器用，皆刻「仇讎未報」字。

translations.literal: Si in youth lost his father; he served his mother filially. On every painting and utensil he carved the characters "Vengeance not yet taken."
translations.idiomatic: Si lost his father young and served his mother with exemplary devotion. On every scroll and vessel he engraved the words "The debt of vengeance is still unpaid."

sentences.zh: 力學兵法，老不廢書，尤喜顏真卿翰墨，曰：「吾慕其人耳。

translations.literal: He vigorously studied military arts; in old age he did not abandon books. He especially loved Yan Zhenqing's calligraphy, saying: "I admire the man, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He studied warfare with discipline and never stopped reading even in old age. He cherished the calligraphy of Yan Zhenqing and said, "It is the man himself I revere.

sentences.zh: 」弟麟，亦有威名，關中號「二姚」。

translations.literal: " His younger brother Lin also had a fierce reputation; within Guanzhong they were called "the Two Yaos."
translations.idiomatic: " His brother Lin was likewise famed for martial prowess; in the Guanzhong region they were known as "the Two Yaos."

sentences.zh: 子雄、古。

translations.literal: Sons: Xiong and Gu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiong and Gu.

sentences.zh: 弟 麟

translations.literal: Younger brother Lin
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Lin

sentences.zh: 麟字君瑞，兄兕攻河州時，俱在兵間。

translations.literal: Lin, courtesy name Junrui—when elder brother Si attacked Hezhou, both were amid the army.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, styled Junrui, fought alongside his elder brother Si during the Hezhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 中矢透骨，鏃留不去，以強弩出之，笑語自若。

translations.literal: An arrow pierced to the bone; the arrowhead remained and would not come out. With a strong crossbow he drew it out, laughing and talking as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow drove through to the bone and the head would not budge. He wrenched it free with a powerful crossbow and went on laughing and chatting as though nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 積功至皇城使，為秦鳳副總管。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit he reached Imperial City Commissioner and served as deputy chief commander of Qinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated service he rose to Imperial City Commissioner and became deputy chief commander of Qinfeng.

sentences.zh: 從李憲討生羌，擒泠雞樸。

translations.literal: Following Li Xian in punishing the Raw Qiang, he captured Leng Jipu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Li Xian he campaigned against the unassimilated Qiang and captured Leng Jipu.

sentences.zh: 再轉東上閣門使、英州刺史。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元豐西討，以涇原副總管從劉昌祚出戰，勝於磨𠼪隘。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng western expedition, as deputy chief commander of Jingyuan he followed Liu Changzuo into battle and was victorious at Moxie Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng western campaigns he served as deputy chief commander of Jingyuan under Liu Changzuo and won a victory at Moxie Pass.

sentences.zh: 轉戰向鳴沙，趨靈州，而高遵裕敗還，降為皇城使、永興軍路鈐轄，復為涇原副總管。

translations.literal: Turning battle toward Mingsha, pressing toward Lingzhou, yet Gao Zunyu was defeated and returned; [Lin] was demoted to Imperial City Commissioner and Controller of the Yongxing Army circuit, then again deputy chief commander of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on toward Mingsha and pressed toward Lingzhou, but when Gao Zunyu's force was beaten back he was demoted to Imperial City Commissioner and controller on the Yongxing Army circuit, then restored as deputy chief commander of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 夏人修貢，且乞蘭會壤土，麟言：「夏人囚其主，王師是征。

translations.literal: The Xia sent tribute and also begged for the Lan and Hui territories. Lin said: "The Xia imprisoned their lord; the royal army was right to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut court resumed tribute and asked for the Lan and Hui lands. Lin argued, "They imprisoned their ruler—our armies were justified in marching.

sentences.zh: 今秉常不廢，即為順命，可因以息兵矣。

translations.literal: Now Bingchang is not removed—that is obedience to the command; one may thereby cease troops.
