translations.idiomatic: Yet Bingchang still holds the throne, so they are obeying the court again. We should take this chance to stand the armies down.

sentences.zh: 獨蘭會不可與。

translations.literal: Only Lan and Hui must not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lan and Hui must not be surrendered.

sentences.zh: 願戒將帥飭邊備，示進討之形，以絕其望。

translations.literal: I wish to warn generals to tighten border defenses and show the form of advancing to punish, thereby cutting off their hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Warn the frontier commanders to tighten defenses and show every sign of a renewed offensive, so their ambitions die on the vine.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 督諸將討堪哥平，經略使盧秉上其功狀，賜金帛六百。

translations.literal: Supervising the generals in punishing Kange Ping, the frontier commissioner Lu Bing submitted his merit report; [Lin] was granted six hundred in gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the generals against Kange Ping; frontier commissioner Lu Bing memorialized his achievements, and the court awarded six hundred strings' worth of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，擢成州團練使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使，曆步軍殿前都虞候、步軍馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou he was promoted to regimentation commissioner of Chengzhou and four-director commander of the Dragon Spirit Guard, passing through vice director of the Palace Front Corps and deputy director of the Foot and Horse Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he was elevated to regimentation commissioner of Chengzhou and four-director commander of the Dragon Spirit Guard, and served in turn as vice director of the Palace Front Corps and deputy director of both the Foot and Horse corps.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，以建武軍節度觀察留後出知渭州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, as military governor and observation commissioner of Jianwu Army he went out to govern Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng year three he left the capital as military governor and observation commissioner of Jianwu Army to govern Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 安燾請留之，曾布曰：「臣嘗訪麟禦邊之策及熙河疆域，俱不能知。

translations.literal: An Yan asked to retain him. Zeng Bu said: "Your subject once inquired of Lin's frontier-defense strategy and the borders of Xihe—he knew neither.
translations.idiomatic: An Yan urged the court to keep him in the capital. Zeng Bu said, "I once asked Lin about frontier strategy and the bounds of Xihe, and he knew nothing of either.

sentences.zh: 願加敕儆，使之盡力。

translations.literal: I wish to add stern admonition, causing him to exert his strength to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Give him a sharp reprimand and make him serve with everything he has.

sentences.zh: 」韓忠彥曰：「奏對語言，非所以責此輩。

translations.literal: " Han Zhongyan said: "Memorial answers and speech are not the way to hold such men accountable.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Zhongyan replied, "You do not make men like this answer for themselves with polished words in audience.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗乃留麟不遣。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhezong then retained Lin and did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Zhezong kept Lin at court and would not release him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜武康軍節度使、殿前副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed military governor of Wukang Army and deputy director of the Palace Front Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made military governor of Wukang Army and deputy director of the Palace Front Corps.

sentences.zh: 王贍取青唐，麟以為朝廷討伐方息肩，奈何復生此大患。

translations.literal: Wang Shan took Qingtang; Lin considered that the court's punitive campaigns had just eased their shoulders—why again bring forth this great calamity?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shan seized Qingtang, Lin warned that the court had only just caught its breath after punitive campaigns—why invite catastrophe again?

sentences.zh: 已而贍果敗。

translations.literal: Before long Shan indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Shan was indeed routed.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，進都指揮使，節度建雄、定武軍，檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong acceded, [Lin] advanced to director of the corps, governed Jianxiong and Dingwu armies, and was made honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Lin rose to director of the corps, held the Jianxiong and Dingwu commands, and received the honorary title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，帝詣其第臨奠，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On his death the emperor went to his residence to mourn in person; posthumously [honored with] Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor came in person to his house to mourn. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 麟為將沈毅持重，不少縱舍。

translations.literal: Lin as general was deep, resolute, and steady, seldom indulging or pardoning.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Lin was grave, steady, and sparing of mercy.

sentences.zh: 宿衛士嘗犯法，詔釋之，麟杖之於庭而後請拒詔之罪，故所至肅然。

translations.literal: Palace guards once violated the law; an edict released them. Lin caned them in the courtyard and only then requested the crime of resisting an edict; therefore wherever he went was solemn.
translations.idiomatic: When palace guards once broke the law, an edict ordered them released. Lin flogged them in the courtyard first, then asked to be punished for defying the edict—so discipline followed him wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 子 雄

translations.literal: Son Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xiong

sentences.zh: 雄字毅夫，少勇鷙有謀，年十八即佐父征伐。

translations.literal: Xiong, courtesy name Yifu—in youth brave, fierce, and scheming; at eighteen he already assisted his father in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Yifu, was fierce and clever from youth; at eighteen he was already fighting at his father's side.

sentences.zh: 從討金湯，以百騎先登奪隘，又成荔原之功。

translations.literal: Following the punitive action against Jintang, with a hundred horsemen he was first to ascend and seize the pass; again he achieved merit at Liyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Jintang he led a hundred horsemen to storm the pass first, and later won distinction at Liyuan as well.

sentences.zh: 韓絳薦其材，閱試延和殿。

translations.literal: Han Jiang recommended his talent; [he was] examined at the Yanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang recommended his abilities, and he was tested at the Yanhe Hall.

sentences.zh: 安南、瀘川之役，皆在軍行。

translations.literal: The campaigns in Annam and Luzhou—both times he marched with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the field in both the Annam and Luzhou campaigns.

sentences.zh: 曆涇原、秦鳳將，駐甘穀城，知通遠鎮戎軍、岷州，官累左騏驥使。

translations.literal: He passed through commands in Jingyuan and Qinfeng, garrisoned Gangu City, governed Tongyuan, Zhenrong Army, and Minzhou; his office accumulated to Left Qiji Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts in Jingyuan and Qinfeng, garrisoned Gangu City, and governed Tongyuan, Zhenrong Army, and Minzhou, rising to Left Qiji Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，渭帥章楶城平夏，雄部熙河兵策援，夏人傾國來，與之鏖鬥，流矢注肩，戰ＴＥ厲，賊引卻，追躡大破之，斬首三千級，俘虜數萬。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng, Wei's commander Zhang Mi fortified Pingxia; Xiong led Xihe troops to support by plan. The Xia came with the whole nation, locked in fierce battle with them; streaming arrows poured into his shoulder; he fought all the harder. The bandits withdrew; pursuing and treading on them he broke them utterly—beheading three thousand ranks, capturing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng, Wei's commander Zhang Mi built up Pingxia Fort. Xiong led Xihe troops to reinforce him. The Tanguts threw their full strength into the fight; arrows rained into his shoulder, yet he fought all the harder. The enemy gave ground; he pursued, crushed them completely, took three thousand heads, and captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 先五日，折可適敗於沒煙，士氣方沮，雄賈勇得雋，諸道始得並力。

translations.literal: Five days earlier Zhe Keshi had been defeated at Moyan; morale was just depressed. Xiong bought courage and won distinction; the various circuits then could combine strength.
translations.idiomatic: Five days before, Zhe Keshi had been beaten at Moyan and spirits were low. Xiong's daring stroke restored confidence, and the various columns could finally fight as one.

sentences.zh: 城成，擢東上閣門使、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: When the fort was completed, he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort stood complete, he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，虜攻平夏，勢銳甚，城幾不守。

translations.literal: The next year the barbarians attacked Pingxia; their momentum was very sharp; the city nearly could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the enemy assaulted Pingxia with crushing force; the city nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 雄與弟古合兵卻之。

translations.literal: Xiong with younger brother Gu united troops and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and his brother Gu joined forces and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 徙知會州，領熙河鈐轄。

translations.literal: Transferred to govern Huizhou; headed Xihe as Controller.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Huizhou and made controller of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 王贍略地青唐，羌人攻湟、鄯，詔雄與苗履援之。

translations.literal: Wang Shan seized territory at Qingtang; the Qiang attacked Huang and Shan. An edict ordered Xiong and Miao Lu to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shan expanded into Qingtang, Qiang forces struck Huang and Shan. The court ordered Xiong and Miao Lu to their relief.

sentences.zh: 邈川方急，雄適至，羌望見塵起，驚而潰。

translations.literal: Miaochuan was just urgent; Xiong happened to arrive; the Qiang seeing dust rise were startled and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Miaochuan was in dire straits when Xiong arrived; the Qiang saw the dust of his columns and broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 圍既解，遂趨鄯州，履後期乃至，贍言蘭溪宗有遺寇，宜悉蕩平之。

translations.literal: Once the siege was lifted, he then pressed toward Shanzhou. Lu was late and only then arrived. Shan said the Lanxizong had remnant bandits and all should be swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted he hurried toward Shanzhou. Miao Lu arrived late. Wang Shan argued that remnant rebels remained among the Lanxizong and should be exterminated.

sentences.zh: 履即往，雄諫不聽，戒所部嚴備以待。

translations.literal: Lu immediately went; Xiong remonstrated but was not heeded, warning his troops to prepare strictly and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Lu marched off at once. Xiong protested in vain and ordered his own men to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 俄而履師退，賊追及，雄整眾迎擊，破之，獻馘二千。

translations.literal: Before long Lu's army retreated; bandits pursued and caught up. Xiong arrayed the host to meet and strike, broke them, and presented two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lu's force fell back with the enemy on its heels. Xiong formed his men, counterattacked, routed them, and sent two thousand heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 哲宗遣中使持詔勞問，徙河州。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong sent a palace envoy bearing an edict of consolation; [Xiong] was moved to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong dispatched a palace envoy with words of praise, and Xiong was transferred to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 種朴戰沒，王贍軍陷敵中，雄自鄯至湟，四戰皆捷，拔出之。

translations.literal: Zhong Pu died in battle; Wang Shan's army was trapped amid the enemy. Xiong from Shan to Huang fought four battles all victorious and pulled them out.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Pu fell in battle and Wang Shan's army was trapped behind enemy lines, Xiong fought four victories from Shan to Huang and brought them out alive.

sentences.zh: 遂築安鄉關，夾河立堡，以護浮梁，通湟水漕運，商旅負販入湟者，始絡繹於道。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built Anxiang Pass, set forts on both banks of the river to protect the floating bridge, opened Huang River grain transport, and merchants carrying goods into Huang for the first time thronged the road.
translations.idiomatic: He then built Anxiang Pass and riverside forts to shield the pontoon bridge, opened grain transport on the Huang River, and for the first time traders packed the road into Huang.

sentences.zh: 加復州防禦使。

translations.literal: Added [honor of] defense commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further honored as defense commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國初，議棄湟州，詔訪雄利害。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong Jingguo, abandoning Huangzhou was debated; an edict asked Xiong the pros and cons.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong Jingguo era the court debated giving up Huangzhou and asked Xiong for his judgment.

sentences.zh: 雄以為可棄，遂以賜趙懷德，徙雄知熙州，進華州觀察使。

translations.literal: Xiong considered it could be abandoned; thereupon it was granted to Zhao Huaide; Xiong was moved to govern Xizhou and advanced to observation commissioner of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong judged the territory expendable; it was granted to Zhao Huaide, Xiong was reassigned to Xizhou, and promoted to observation commissioner of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡京用王厚復河湟，治棄地罪，停雄官，光州居住。

translations.literal: Cai Jing employed Wang Hou to recover He and Huang; punishing the crime of abandoning territory, Xiong's office was suspended and he resided at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing sent Wang Hou to retake He and Huang, Xiong was punished for surrendering land—stripped of office and sent to live at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，得自便。

translations.literal: In the third year he was allowed to go where he wished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was permitted to move freely.

sentences.zh: 後論為責輕，復竄金州。

translations.literal: Later it was judged the penalty too light; again he was banished to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics deemed the sentence too mild, and he was exiled again to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃聽歸。

translations.literal: The next year he was at last allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was finally allowed to come home.

sentences.zh: 高永年死，西寧諸戍阻絕，起雄權經略熙河、安輯復新邊使。

translations.literal: When Gao Yongnian died and the Xining garrisons were cut off, Xiong was raised to acting frontier commissioner of Xihe and commissioner for pacifying and restoring the new border.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Yongnian's death left the Xining posts isolated, Xiong was recalled as acting frontier commissioner of Xihe and commissioner for settling the new border.

sentences.zh: 知滄州，加捧日、天武四廂都指揮使，復為熙州，遷安德軍節度觀察留後、步軍副都指揮使，拜武康軍節度使。

translations.literal: Governing Cangzhou, added four-director commander of the Sun-and-Heaven Guard, again [governed] Xizhou, transferred to military governor and observation commissioner of Ande Army and deputy director of the Foot Corps, appointed military governor of Wukang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Cangzhou, was made four-director commander of the Sun-and-Heaven Guard, returned to Xizhou, rose to military governor and observation commissioner of Ande Army and deputy director of the Foot Corps, and was appointed military governor of Wukang Army.

sentences.zh: 召詣闕，為中太一宮使。

translations.literal: Summoned to the court, [he became] commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Called to court, he became commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 引疾納節鉞，改左金吾衛上將軍，又以武康節知熙州。

translations.literal: Citing illness he returned the seal and axe; changed to senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, again with Wukang command knowing Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading illness he surrendered his command seal, was made senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and once more held Wukang command while governing Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 熙河十八年間更十六帥，唯雄三至，凡六年。

translations.literal: In eighteen years at Xihe there were sixteen commanders in all; only Xiong came three times—for six years in total.
translations.idiomatic: In eighteen years on the Xihe frontier sixteen commanders rotated through; Xiong alone served three tours totaling six years.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以檢校司空、奉甯軍節度使致仕。

translations.literal: Before long, with honorary Minister of Works and military governor of Fengning Army he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he retired with the honorary rank of Minister of Works and the Fengning Army command.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈開府儀同三司，諡武憲。

translations.literal: On his death, posthumously [honored with] Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies; posthumous title Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 子 古

translations.literal: Son Gu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gu

sentences.zh: 既而議和，金兵退，詔古與種師中、折彥質、範瓊等領兵十余萬護送之。

translations.literal: Before long peace was negotiated; Jin troops withdrew. An edict [ordered] Gu with Zhong Shizhong, Zhe Yanzhi, Fan Qiong, and others to lead more than a hundred thousand troops to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was struck and the Jin armies withdrew, the court ordered Gu, together with Zhong Shizhong, Zhe Yanzhi, Fan Qiong, and others, to escort them with an army of more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 粘罕陷隆德府，以古為河東制置，種師中副之。

translations.literal: Zhanhan captured Longde Prefecture; Gu was made Hebei frontier commissioner with Zhong Shizhong as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhanhan took Longde Prefecture, Gu was appointed Hebei frontier commissioner with Zhong Shizhong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 古總兵援太原，師中援中山、河間諸郡。

translations.literal: Gu commanded troops to relieve Taiyuan; Shizhong relieved Zhongshan and the Hejian commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Gu led the force to relieve Taiyuan while Shizhong reinforced Zhongshan and the Hejian region.

sentences.zh: 粘罕圍太原，內外不相通。

translations.literal: Zhanhan besieged Taiyuan; inside and outside did not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanhan besieged Taiyuan until the city was severed from the outside world.

sentences.zh: 古進兵復隆德府、威勝軍，厄南北關，與金人戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: Gu advanced troops and recovered Longde Prefecture and Weisheng Army, blocked the northern and southern passes, fought with the Jin people—each side had victories and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Gu marched forward, retook Longde Prefecture and Weisheng Army, and held the northern and southern passes. Battles with the Jin swayed back and forth without a clear victor.

sentences.zh: 太原圍不解，詔古與師中掎角，師中進次平定軍，乘勝復壽陽、榆次等縣。

translations.literal: Taiyuan's siege was not lifted; an edict [ordered] Gu and Shizhong to coordinate like pincers. Shizhong advanced and halted at Pingding Army, riding victory to recover Shouyang, Yuci, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan remained under siege; the court ordered Gu and Shizhong to coordinate pincer attacks. Shizhong moved up to Pingding Army and, pressing his advantage, recovered Shouyang, Yuci, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 朝廷數遣使趣戰，師中約古及張灝兩軍齊進，而二人失期不至。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly sent envoys urging battle. Shizhong arranged with Gu and Zhang Hao for both armies to advance together, but the two men missed the appointed time and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoy after envoy demanding action. Shizhong arranged a joint advance with Gu and Zhang Hao, but both columns failed to appear on time.

sentences.zh: 師中回趨榆次，兵敗而死。

translations.literal: Shizhong turned back toward Yuci; the army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong wheeled back toward Yuci, his army was broken, and he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 金人進兵迎古，遇於盤陀，古兵潰，退保隆德。

translations.literal: Jin troops advanced to meet Gu; they encountered at Panto; Gu's army routed and retreated to hold Longde.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army marched to intercept Gu at Panto. His force collapsed and fell back to defend Longde.

sentences.zh: 詔以解潛代之。

translations.literal: An edict [ordered] Xie Qian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced him with Xie Qian.

sentences.zh: 古之屯威勝軍也，帳下統制官焦安節妄傳寇至以動軍情，既又勸古遁去，故兩郡皆潰。

translations.literal: When Gu was encamped at Weisheng Army, the regimental officer under his tent Jiao Anjie falsely reported bandits arrived to stir the army's mood; afterward he also urged Gu to flee—therefore both commanderies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: While Gu was stationed at Weisheng Army, his regimental officer Jiao Anjie spread a false alarm of enemy attack to panic the troops, then urged Gu to run. Both districts unraveled.

sentences.zh: 李綱召安節，斬于瓊林苑。

translations.literal: Li Gang summoned Anjie and beheaded him at the Qiongl Forest Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang had Anjie summoned and executed him in the Qiongl Forest Garden.

sentences.zh: 中丞陳過庭奏古罪不可恕，詔安置廣州。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Chen Guoting memorialized that Gu's crimes could not be forgiven; an edict [ordered him] settled at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chief censor Chen Guoting memorialized that Gu's offenses were unpardonable, and the court banished him to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 燧初穴貝州城時，為叛兵所傷，同行卒劉順救之得免。

translations.literal: When Gu first tunneled into Beizhou city, he was wounded by rebel soldiers; fellow soldier Liu Shun saved him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu first dug through into Beizhou city during the siege, rebel soldiers wounded him; the soldier Liu Shun pulled him out and he survived.

sentences.zh: 及貴，順已死，訪恤其家甚至。

translations.literal: When he had risen high, Shun was already dead; he inquired after and comforted his family to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: After he had risen to high rank Liu Shun was already dead; Gu sought out his family and provided for them generously.

sentences.zh: 故人妻子貧不能活者，一切收養之。

translations.literal: Old friends' wives and children who were poor and could not live—he took them all in and raised them.
translations.idiomatic: He took in and supported every impoverished wife and child left behind by old comrades.

sentences.zh: 人推其義。

translations.literal: People praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: People honored him for his loyalty and kindness.

sentences.zh: 劉舜卿

translations.literal: Liu Shunqing
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shunqing

sentences.zh: 劉舜卿。

translations.literal: Liu Shunqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shunqing.

sentences.zh: 字希元，開封人。

translations.literal: Courtesy name Xiyuan; a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Xiyuan, and he was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父鈞，監鎮戎兵馬，慶曆中，與子堯卿戰死于好水。

translations.literal: His father Jun supervised the troops and horses at Zhenrong; in the Qingli era he fought at Haoshui and died together with Zhong Yaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Jun had been overseer of cavalry and horses at Zhenrong; during the Qingli era he fought at Haoshui and was killed there alongside Zhong Yaoqing.

sentences.zh: 舜卿年十歲，錄為供奉官，曆昌州駐泊都監。

translations.literal: Shunqing at age ten was enrolled as a Palace Attendant and served in turn as Coastal Patrol Commander stationed at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunqing was ten, the court enrolled him as a Palace Attendant; he later served as Coastal Patrol Commander stationed at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 諭降瀘水蠻八百人，誅其桀鼇驁者。

translations.literal: He persuaded eight hundred Lushui tribesmen to surrender and executed the violent and defiant among them.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded eight hundred Lushui tribesmen to submit and put to death those who were violent and unruly.

sentences.zh: 知水洛城。

translations.literal: He governed Shuilo City.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shuilo City.

sentences.zh: 神宗經略西邊，近臣薦其能，召問狀，對曰：「自元昊稱臣，秦中不復戒嚴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong was planning the western frontier, close advisors recommended his ability; summoned to report on conditions, he replied: "Since Yuanhao submitted as a vassal, the Qin region has no longer been on war footing.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shenzong was preparing operations on the western frontier, court intimates recommended him for his competence. Summoned to give an account of the situation, he answered: "Ever since Yuanhao submitted as a vassal, the Qin heartland has no longer lived under constant alert.

sentences.zh: 今宜先自治。

translations.literal: Now we should first put our own house in order.
translations.idiomatic: We ought first to set our own affairs in order.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之，命訓京東將兵。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved and ordered him to drill the troops of the eastern capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased and ordered him to train the generals and troops of the eastern capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 一年，入閱於內殿，帝歎曰：「坐作有度，其可用也。

translations.literal: After one year he was inspected in the inner hall; the Emperor sighed and said: "Their sitting and rising have measure—they can be used.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was reviewed in the inner hall. The Emperor sighed and said, "Their drill has discipline—they will serve.

sentences.zh: 爾無忘世讎，勉思忠孝，期以盡敵。

translations.literal: Do not forget the feud handed down from your forebears; strive in loyalty and filial piety and aim to destroy the enemy utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Do not forget the blood feud your families owe; strive in loyalty and filial duty and seek to annihilate the foe.

sentences.zh: 」舜卿泣謝，即日加通事舍人。

translations.literal: " Shunqing wept in thanks, and that same day he was promoted to Imperial Protocol Officer.
translations.idiomatic: " Shunqing wept as he thanked him, and that same day was promoted to Imperial Protocol Officer.

sentences.zh: 環慶有警，詔帥長安兵赴之，乃單騎馳往慶州，至則難已解。

translations.literal: When Huanqing circuit raised an alarm, an edict ordered him to lead Chang'an troops to the scene; he rode alone to Qingzhou, and when he arrived the crisis was already over.
translations.idiomatic: When Huanqing circuit came under threat, the court ordered him to lead Chang'an troops thither; he galloped to Qingzhou alone and found the danger already past by the time he arrived.

sentences.zh: 知原州，改秦鳳鈐轄。

translations.literal: He governed Yuan Prefecture and was transferred to Qinfeng military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yuan Prefecture, then was reassigned as Qinfeng military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 襲擊西市城，先登有功，遷皇城副使。

translations.literal: In a raid on Xishi City he was first to scale the walls with merit and was promoted Deputy Commissioner of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: In an assault on Xishi City he was first over the wall with distinction and was promoted Deputy Commissioner of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 久之，知代州，加客省副使。

translations.literal: After a long interval he governed Daizhou and was given the additional title Vice Commissioner of the Office for Receiving Foreign Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he governed Daizhou and received the additional title Vice Commissioner of the Office for Receiving Foreign Guests.

sentences.zh: 遼遣諜盜西關鎖，舜卿密易舊鑰鐍而大之。

translations.literal: The Liao sent a spy to steal the west gate lock; Shunqing secretly replaced the old lock and made the new one larger.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao dispatched a spy to steal the west gate lock; Shunqing quietly swapped the old lock for a larger one.

sentences.zh: 數日，虜以鎖來歸，舜卿曰：「吾未嘗亡鎖也。

translations.literal: Days later the barbarians returned with the lock; Shunqing said: "I have never lost a lock.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the Khitan came back with the lock. Shunqing said, "I have never lost a lock.

sentences.zh: 」引視，納之不能受，遂慚去，誅諜者。

translations.literal: " He showed it to them; it would not fit, so they left in shame, and he executed the spy.
translations.idiomatic: " When he showed them the gate, the lock would not seat; they withdrew in embarrassment, and he had the spy put to death.

sentences.zh: 轉西上閣門使、知雄州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and governed Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Western Upper Gate Commissioner and appointed prefect of Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始視事，或告契丹遊騎大集，請甲以俟，舜卿不為動，乃妄也。

translations.literal: When he first took office, someone reported that Khitan raiders were massing in strength and asked for armor to stand ready; Shunqing was unmoved—it proved to be false.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his tenure someone warned that Khitan patrols were gathering in force and begged for arms to await them; Shunqing did not stir, and the report proved empty.

sentences.zh: 契丹系州民，檄索之，不聽。

translations.literal: The Khitan seized a man of the prefecture and demanded him by proclamation; Shunqing refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan bound up a local man and demanded his return by official notice, Shunqing would not comply.

sentences.zh: 會有使者至，因捕取其一以相當，必得釋乃遣。

translations.literal: When an envoy arrived, he seized one of theirs in exchange and would not release him until their captive was freed.
translations.idiomatic: On the arrival of an envoy he took one of their men in turn and would not send him back until the townsman was released.

sentences.zh: 在雄六年，恩信周浹。

translations.literal: During six years at Xiong his kindness and trust reached everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: For six years at Xiong his grace and good faith ran deep on every side.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，進龍神衛四廂都指揮使、高州刺史、知熙州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was promoted Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Divine Guard, Prefect of Gaozhou, and prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou reign he rose to Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Divine Guard, was enfeoffed as Prefect of Gaozhou, and governed Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夏人聚兵天都，連西羌鬼章青宜結，先城洮州，將大舉入寇，舜卿欲乘其未集擊之，會諸將議方略。

translations.literal: The Tanguts massed troops at Tiandu, joined with the Western Qiang chieftain Gui Zhang Qingyijie, and first fortified Taozhou, intending a major invasion; Shunqing wished to strike before they assembled and convened the generals to discuss strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanguts gathered at Tiandu in league with the Western Qiang chieftain Gui Zhang Qingyijie, fortified Taozhou first, and prepared a large-scale raid. Shunqing wanted to hit them before their forces converged and called the commanders together to plan.

sentences.zh: 使姚兕部洮西，領武勝兵合河州熟羌搗講珠城，遣人間道焚河橋以絕西援；

translations.literal: He sent Yao Si to command west of the Tao, leading Wusheng troops with allied tribes from Hezhou to strike Jiangzhu City, and dispatched men by hidden paths to burn the river bridge and cut off western relief.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned Yao Si to the west of the Tao with Wusheng troops and Hezhou allied tribes to raid Jiangzhu City, and sent men by secret routes to burn the river bridge and sever aid from the west.

sentences.zh: 種誼部洮東，由哥龍谷宵濟邦金川，黎明，至臨洮城下，一鼓克之，俘鬼章並首領九人，斬馘數千計。

translations.literal: Chong Yi commanded east of the Tao; by night he crossed the Bangjin River through Gelong Valley, and at dawn, below Lintao City, took it at the first assault; he captured Gui Zhang together with nine chieftains, and the heads and kills numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Yi took the east of the Tao, crossed the Bangjin River by night through Gelong Valley, and at dawn was beneath Lintao City, which fell at the first rush. He took Gui Zhang and nine other leaders captive, and the slain ran to several thousand.

sentences.zh: 遷馬軍都虞候，再遷徐州觀察使、步軍副都指揮使、知渭州。

translations.literal: Shunqing was promoted Commander of the Guard Cavalry and again promoted Observation Commissioner of Xuzhou, Deputy Commander of the Infantry, and prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Commander of the Guard Cavalry, then again to Observation Commissioner of Xuzhou, Deputy Commander of the Infantry, and prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召還宿衛，未上道，卒，贈奉國軍節度使，諡曰毅敏。

translations.literal: Recalled to palace guard duty, before he had set out on the road he died; posthumously [honored as] Military Commissioner of the Fengguo Army; posthumous title Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him to palace guard service, but he died before he could depart. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Military Commissioner of the Fengguo Army, with the posthumous name Yimin.

sentences.zh: 舜卿知書，曉吏事，謹文法，善料敵，著名北州。

translations.literal: Shunqing was literate, understood administrative affairs, was strict in law, skilled at gauging the enemy, and famed in the northern circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing was learned, understood governance, enforced the statutes carefully, read the enemy well, and was renowned throughout the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 宋守約

translations.literal: Song Shouyue
translations.idiomatic: Song Shouyue

sentences.zh: 宋守約，開封酸棗人。

translations.literal: Song Shouyue was a man of Suanzao in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shouyue was a native of Suanzao in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以父任為左班殿直，至河北緣邊安撫副使，選知恩州。

translations.literal: Through his father's appointment he became a Left Guard Attendant of the Inner Hall, rose to Deputy Frontier Pacification Commissioner of Hebei, and was selected to govern En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary appointment he entered service as a Left Guard Attendant of the Inner Hall, rose to Deputy Frontier Pacification Commissioner on the Hebei border, and was chosen to govern En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仁宗諭以亂後撫禦之意，對曰：「恩與他郡等耳，而為守者猶以反側待之，故人心不自安。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong instructed him on the intent to pacify and defend after the rebellion; he replied: "En is no different from other prefectures, yet those who govern still treat the people as restive, so hearts are not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong explained how he should reassure the region after the uprising. Shouyue answered: "En is like any other prefecture, yet its magistrates still treat the people as if they might turn again, and so no one feels secure.

sentences.zh: 臣願盡力。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to exert himself to the full.
translations.idiomatic: I will do all I can.

sentences.zh: 」徙益州路鈐轄，累遷文州刺史、康州團練使、知雄州，曆龍神衛、捧日天武都指揮使，馬步殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yizhou Circuit military commissioner, was promoted in succession to Prefect of Wenzhou, Regimental Commissioner of Kangzhou, and prefect of Xiong Prefecture, and served as Commander of the Dragon Divine Guard and the Sunbearing and Sky Martial Guards and as Commander of the Guard Cavalry and Infantry of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Yizhou Circuit military commissioner, rose through Prefect of Wenzhou and Regimental Commissioner of Kangzhou to prefect of Xiong Prefecture, and held commands over the Dragon Divine Guard and the Sunbearing and Sky Martial Guards and over the palace cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 入宿衛，遷洋州觀察使。

translations.literal: He entered palace guard service and was promoted Observation Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the palace guard and was promoted Observation Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 衛兵以給粟陳嘩噪，執政將付有司治，守約曰：「禦軍安用文法！

translations.literal: The guard soldiers clamored over grain rations; the chief ministers were about to hand the matter to the judicial offices, but Shouyue said: "What use are written laws for guarding the army!
translations.idiomatic: The guard troops raised an uproar over their grain issue; the chief ministers meant to refer the case to the courts, but Shouyue said, "What use is paperwork in commanding soldiers!

sentences.zh: 」遣一牙校語之曰：「天子太倉粟，不請何為？

translations.literal: He sent a staff officer to tell them: "It is the Son of Heaven's granary grain—why not request it properly?
translations.idiomatic: He sent a staff officer to say to them, "This is grain from the Son of Heaven's storehouses—why not ask for it as you should?

sentences.zh: 我不貸汝。

translations.literal: I will not spare you.
translations.idiomatic: I will show you no leniency.

sentences.zh: 」眾懼而聽命。

translations.literal: The crowd feared and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The men feared him and submitted.

sentences.zh: 進步軍副都指揮使、威武軍留後。

translations.literal: He was promoted Deputy Commander of the Infantry and Regent of the Weiwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Deputy Commander of the Infantry and Regent of the Weiwu Army.

sentences.zh: 神宗以禁旅驕惰，為簡練之法，屯營可並者並之。

translations.literal: Because the palace guard troops had grown proud and lax, Emperor Shenzong instituted methods of drill and consolidation, merging encampments where they could be merged.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong, finding the palace guards arrogant and slack, set down rules for training and consolidation and merged camps wherever merger was possible.

sentences.zh: 守約率先推行，約束嚴峻，士始怨終服。

translations.literal: Shouyue was the first to carry them out; his discipline was severe; at first the troops resented it, but in the end they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue took the lead in enforcing them with stern discipline; the men grumbled at first but came to accept it.

sentences.zh: 或言其持軍太急，帝密戒之，對曰：「臣為陛下明紀律，不忍使恩出於臣，而怨歸陛下。

translations.literal: Some said he held the army too tightly; the Emperor secretly warned him; he replied: "Your servant clarifies discipline for Your Majesty; I cannot bear that favor should seem to come from me while resentment falls on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When some complained that he drove the troops too hard, the Emperor quietly cautioned him. Shouyue answered, "I am setting discipline clear for Your Majesty; I would not have kindness credited to me and blame fall on the throne.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之，欲擢置樞府，宰相難之，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved; he wished to elevate him to the Privy Council, but the chief ministers objected, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and meant to place him in the Privy Council, but the chief ministers resisted and the promotion went no further.

sentences.zh: 故事，當郊之歲，先期籍士卒之兇悍者，配下軍以警眾，當受糧而倩人代負者罰，久而浸弛，守約悉舉行之。

translations.literal: By precedent, in the year of the suburban sacrifice, violent soldiers were registered in advance and assigned to lower armies as a warning to the rest; those who hired others to carry their grain allotment were punished—over time this had lapsed, and Shouyue restored it in full.
translations.idiomatic: Custom held that in a suburban-sacrifice year the most unruly soldiers were listed beforehand and posted to inferior units as a warning, and men who paid others to haul their grain rations were penalized; the practice had long slipped, and Shouyue enforced every part of it again.

sentences.zh: 所居肅然無人聲，至蟬噪於庭亦擊去，人以為過。

translations.literal: His residence was so quiet that no human voice was heard; even cicadas chirping in the courtyard were driven away—people thought it excessive.
translations.idiomatic: His household was so hushed that scarcely a voice was heard; he even had cicadas in the courtyard chased off, and many judged him extreme.

sentences.zh: 蒞職十年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: After ten years in office he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He held his post for ten years and died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈安武軍節度使，諡曰勤毅。

translations.literal: Posthumously [honored as] Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army; posthumous title Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army, with the posthumous name Qinyi.

sentences.zh: 子 球

translations.literal: Son Qiu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Qiu

sentences.zh: 子球，以蔭幹當禮賓院。

translations.literal: His son Qiu served in the Court of Diplomatic Reception through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiu entered the Court of Diplomatic Reception by inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 條秦、川券馬四弊，群牧使用其議，馬商便之。

translations.literal: He memorialized four abuses in the Qin and Sichuan voucher-horse system; the Pastoral Offices adopted his proposal, to the benefit of horse merchants.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out four abuses in the Qin and Sichuan ticket-horse system; the Pastoral Offices took up his plan, and horse traders found relief.

sentences.zh: 再使高麗，密訪山川形勢、風俗好尚，使還，圖紀上之，神宗稱善，進通事舍人。

translations.literal: Twice envoy to Goryeo, he secretly surveyed terrain and customs; on his return he submitted an illustrated record; Emperor Shenzong praised it and promoted him to Imperial Protocol Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Sent twice to Goryeo, he quietly mapped mountains, rivers, and local ways; when he returned he presented an illustrated report. Emperor Shenzong commended it and promoted him to Imperial Protocol Officer.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，告哀契丹，至，則使易吉服，球曰：「通和歲久，憂患是同，大國安則為之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, he went to announce mourning to the Khitan; on arrival they wished him to change out of mourning dress; Qiu said: "We have been at peace for many years and share the same grief; if the great state were at ease we would comply.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor's death he carried the mourning notice to the Khitan; when he arrived they pressed him to put off mourning garb. Qiu said, "We have lived in peace for long years and mourn the same loss; were your great state itself untroubled, we would do as you ask.

translations.idiomatic: " The Khitan could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 積遷西上閣門使、樞密副都承旨。

translations.literal: By accumulated promotion he became Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Deputy Receiver of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in time to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Deputy Receiver of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 為人謹密，朝日所聞上語，雖家人不以告。

translations.literal: As a man he was careful and close-mouthed; what he heard from the Emperor each day in court, even his family he did not tell.
translations.idiomatic: He was discreet to a fault: whatever the Emperor said to him at court each day, he would not repeat even to his own household.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自郝質至宋守約，皆恂直忠篤，為一時名將。

translations.literal: The commentators say: From Hao Zhi down to Song Shouyue, all were straightforward, loyal, and steadfast—generals famed in their day.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators write: From Hao Zhi through Song Shouyue, each was honest, loyal, and steadfast—a famed commander of the age.

sentences.zh: 遭世承平，邊疆少警，擁節旄，立殿陛，高爵重祿，以壽考終，宜也。

translations.literal: They lived in an era of sustained peace; border alarms were few; they bore imperial banners and stood on the palace steps; with high rank and heavy stipends they ended their lives in full old age—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: They came of age in long peace, when the frontier seldom flared; they held command seals and stood before the throne, enjoyed lofty rank and rich stipends, and died at a ripe old age—which was only right.

sentences.zh: 姚氏世用武奮，兕與弟麟並有威名，關中號「二姚」。

translations.literal: The Yao clan for generations excelled in arms; Si and his younger brother Lin both won awe-inspiring names; within the Pass they were called "the Two Yaos."
translations.idiomatic: The Yao house had risen by martial merit for generations; Si and his brother Lin both carried formidable reputations, and in the Guanzhong region people spoke of "the Two Yaos."

sentences.zh: 兕之子雄，亦以戰功至節度使，而古竟以敗貶，其才否可見已。

translations.literal: Si's son Xiong also rose through battle merit to military commissioner, yet Gu in the end was demoted after defeat—their talents, or lack of them, are plain enough.
translations.idiomatic: Si's son Xiong likewise fought his way to a military commissioner's post, while Gu ended in defeat and disgrace—the contrast in their gifts could hardly be clearer.
